title: Multi-visit vehicle routing for earthwork hauling: Flow-based formulation and model-driven heuristic
abstract: Earthwork hauling in large-scale construction projects involves repeated vehicle movements between cut and fill nodes, with overall performance typically measured by the system makespan. We study a minimum-makespan cut-and-fill problem and formulate it as a multi-visit arc-flow (MVAF) mixed-integer linear program. The MVAF formulation explicitly captures repeated vehicle movements while avoiding node splitting for multi-unit supply and demand. To ensure global route connectivity under multi-visit routing, we propose two subtour elimination approaches tailored to the MVAF structure. Exploiting problem characteristics, we derive two lower bounds on the makespan that capture unavoidable time requirements imposed by supply–demand patterns and fleet size. For medium- and large-scale instances, we propose a model-driven bottleneck-based fix-and-optimize heuristic (BFOH), which iteratively re-optimizes a small, tightly coupled subset of vehicles centered on the bottleneck vehicle. Computational experiments indicate that the proposed MVAF formulation achieves favorable computational performance and that the proposed lower bounds are tight. BFOH achieves near-optimal solutions for small-scale instances and consistently outperforms the benchmark model in solution quality within limited computational time for medium- and large-scale instances.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: A deviation-based demand-responsive bus service adjustment strategy for same-platform transfers with autonomous rail rapid transit
abstract: In recent years, the Autonomous Rail Rapid Transit (ART) system, which operates on “virtual tracks”, has been adopted in many cities considering its higher flexibility and lower operating and maintenance cost compared to the traditional metro system. However, a persistent challenge lies in the missing coordination between the ART services and the conventional bus services, frequently resulting in excessively long transfer distance and waiting time for passengers. To address this issue, this study proposes a deviation-based demand-responsive bus service adjustment strategy to facilitate transfers between the bus and ART systems. Under this strategy, when transfer requests are triggered by passengers via devices installed on buses or ART platforms, a bus adjusts its route to enter the ART station platform, thereby enabling same-platform transfers. The proposed mechanism synchronizes bus arrival and departure times with ART schedules to avoid disruptions to ART operations. Furthermore, buses execute these deviations without skipping any scheduled stops to minimize adverse impacts on non-transferring passengers. To further enhance operational efficiency and realism, conditional stop control and holding control strategies are incorporated, along with time-varying traffic conditions. A mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model is formulated to jointly minimize both passengers’ and operators’ time. The model is decomposed into two subproblems, and solved using a hybrid Gurobi − Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (GALNS) algorithm. The proposed model and algorithm are validated through a real-world case study in Yibin, China. Promising numerical results indicate that, by adopting the proposed deviation-based demand-responsive strategy, the total time decreases by 1.12%, 0.42%, 21.75%, and 23.48%, respectively, compared to solutions without considering demand responsiveness, control strategies, route deviation, and any strategy. The proposed bus service adjustment strategy provides a valuable guidance on improving the flexibility of conventional bus operations and enhancing the convenience of transfers between the bus and ART systems.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Navigating uncertainty in maritime decarbonization: a multi-risk framework for fuel–technology decisions
abstract: Maritime transport faces growing pressure to align with global net-zero targets, yet investment and operational decisions remain constrained by uncertainty surrounding alternative fuels and decarbonization technologies. Most existing assessments rely on static assumptions and do not capture how transition risks change in different scenarios or interact across political, economic, and technical dimensions. This study develops a multi-risk framework that evaluates six alternative fuels and a broad suite of energy-saving technologies by combining the Entropy Weight Method with Monte Carlo simulation. The framework not only generates risk indices and ranges but also projects the shifting profiles under multiple regulatory and market scenarios from 2025 to 2050. The results show that dominant risk drivers shift over time. Economic factors strongly influence near-term choices, while political and regulatory uncertainties become increasingly important as net-zero regulations tighten. The analysis also identifies a two-stage pattern in technology risks, where early risks are shaped by maturity constraints and later risks are shaped mainly by cost competitiveness. These varying risks create distinct trade-offs between affordability, risk exposure, and well-to-wake emission reduction. From the perspective of the individual performance of fuels and technologies, biofuels and operational measures support lower risk transitions in the short term, while green hydrogen and onboard carbon capture system may become attractive in stricter future policy environments because of their high emission-reduction potential. The study also develops a scenario-based combination evaluation framework to identify the optimal combined fuel-technology pathways under different decision supports for cost, risk, and emission reduction. The framework provides actionable evidence for shipowners, investors, and regulators seeking resilient pathways toward net-zero maritime transport.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Data-driven optimization of a mixed fleet of drones and human couriers for on-demand delivery under uncertainty
abstract: On-demand delivery, which allows consumers to receive purchases quickly after ordering, is becoming increasingly prevalent. While human couriers are commonly used for deliveries, they often lead to higher costs and longer delivery times. Drones can help overcome these limitations but have a shorter range compared to human couriers. Therefore, utilizing a mixed fleet of drones and human couriers offers an effective solution for fast, cost-efficient, and reliable on-demand delivery. This paper focuses on an on-demand delivery system in which a mixed fleet of drones and human couriers collects parcels from a central hub and delivers them to parcel lockers across multiple regions throughout a day, under uncertain parcel demand. We propose a two-stage Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model to jointly optimize the allocation and operation of drones and human couriers in the face of demand uncertainty. We propose reformulation techniques to transform the model into a tractable form. To enhance computational efficiency, we develop an L-shaped algorithm and an alternating direction algorithm. Out-of-sample results based on real-world data highlight the benefits of employing DRO approach. Additionally, we reveal that a mixed fleet outperforms using only drones or only human couriers, with drones prioritized for deliveries and serving as the dominant role, while human couriers play a supplementary role. We also examine how the performance of drones and human couriers varies with changes in several key system parameters.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Customer digital-intelligent transformation and suppliers’ new quality productivity: evidence from supply chain spillovers
abstract: Digital and intelligent technologies are beginning to alter the way major customers interact with upstream suppliers. Beyond improving customers’ own operations, these technologies may also change how demand information, transaction data, and innovation resources move across vertical supply chains. This paper examines this possibility by studying whether customer digital-intelligent transformation (CDIT) is associated with suppliers’ New Quality Productivity (NQP), defined as a structural upgrading of production capability that goes beyond conventional input–output efficiency and innovation-output efficiency. Based on supplier–customer matched data for Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2022, the evidence shows a positive relationship between customers’ digital upgrading and the productivity quality of upstream suppliers. The finding remains stable after using alternative measures, addressing endogeneity, correcting sample-selection bias, and changing empirical specifications. Mechanism analysis indicates that CDIT contributes to supplier upgrading by improving supply–demand alignment, easing financing and transaction frictions, and strengthening digital-intelligent innovation collaboration. The effect is stronger among large suppliers, state-owned suppliers, and firms more dependent on major customers. Overall, the study develops a customer-driven vertical productivity reconfiguration framework, showing how digitally transformed customers reorganize information, transaction, capital, and knowledge flows across customer–supplier relationships and convert firm-level digital capabilities into suppliers’ NQP.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Hybrid quantum AI in logistics and operations management: Operational fit and strategic value
abstract: Logistics optimization and operations management increasingly depend on artificial intelligence and quantum computing to address complex, time-sensitive planning problems. Existing research has focused mainly on algorithmic benchmarks or speculative quantum advantage, while offering limited insight into how Hybrid Quantum AI creates organizational value under current hardware constraints. This study advances theory by integrating Information Processing Theory (IPT) with the Dynamic Capabilities View (DCV), demonstrating how Hybrid Quantum AI architectures generate organizational value despite the current absence of quantum advantage. Using a case analysis of Malaysia Airlines Cargo (MAB Kargo), it is shown how combining AI-driven data structuring with quantum-enhanced optimization can close critical information-processing gaps and support the development of sensing, seizing, and transforming capabilities. Empirically, this hybrid system achieved an 83% reduction in planning time and a 5% increase in capacity utilization. These findings demonstrate that the current value of quantum computing in logistics lies not in outperforming classical solvers, but in enabling modular, future-ready architectures that improve operational fit today and build strategic agility over time. The study contributes to management and information systems research by explaining “quantum readiness” as an organizational capability enabled by modular digital infrastructure, offering practical guidance for digitization roadmaps and computational investment decisions in next-generation logistics.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: The impact of ESG performance on trade credit: the role of operations and supply chain management factors
abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices have increasingly garnered attention on a global scale, highlighting the importance of understanding the potential consequences of ESG performance. The objective of this study is to examine the impact of a firm's ESG performance on the behaviors of suppliers, with a particular emphasis on the trade credit provided by these suppliers. Furthermore, this research also analyzes operations and supply chain management (OSCM) factors such as operational efficiency (OE), supplier concentration (SC), and R&D intensity (R&D), which may serve to moderate this relationship. To achieve these goals, we perform a secondary data analysis encompassing 2,046 listed companies in Chinese manufacturing industries from 2018 to 2023 and find that the performance of corporations in terms of ESG displays an inverted U-shaped correlation with trade credit. Moreover, OE and R&D intensity steepen the inverted U-shape and shift the turning point to the left, while SC flattens the inverted U-shape and also shifts the turning point to the left. These findings suggest that ESG has important logistics and supply chain consequences because it shapes suppliers' willingness to provide the short-term financing that helps stabilize procurement, production, and delivery activities. In light of these findings, we provide a noteworthy contribution to the existing literature on buyer–supplier relationships and logistics fulfilment presenting important implications for both researchers and practitioners in the domain of OSCM.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Optimization of urban reverse logistics networks in express packaging recycling
abstract: The volume of express packaging waste continues to surge, with the vast majority destined for landfills or incineration. Efficient recovery via reverse logistics is often severely hindered by the high dispersion of waste generation nodes and the complex transport networks in high-density urban environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes decentralized and centralized sorting strategies for express packaging waste, with their effectiveness being evaluated and compared. A multi-echelon transportation network is developed and optimized, which connects express delivery points (EDPs), waste transfer stations (WTSs), recycling centers (RCs), and landfills (LFs). Within this multi-echelon network, the study develops a GIS-integrated sequential optimization methodology to solve the multi-echelon, multi-depot, split-delivery vehicle routing problem (ME-MD-SDVRP). To handle the computational complexity of the large-scale urban environment, the global problem is decomposed into a series of MD-SDVRP sub-problems and solved through a multi-stage sequential HSA algorithm. We design a specialized saturate-first decoding strategy to maximize vehicle capacity and handle the fragmented nature of express packaging waste. In a case study of Hong Kong, the locations of over 600 EDPs from major express companies (e.g., HKSHIP Express, Cainiao Express) are geocoded and clustered utilizing an improved K-means algorithm. To ensure modeling accuracy that reflects real-world traffic patterns, empirical traffic data (i.e., time and distance between all node pairs) collected over a 30-day period is integrated into the model. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed HSA algorithm achieves an optimal balance between solution quality and convergence speed relative to exact methods and classical heuristics. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis and baseline capacity evaluations are conducted to identify the optimal vehicle configuration, establishing a foundation for subsequent optimized-capacity experiments. Overall, this study provides a practical decision-making framework for reverse logistics, delivering scalable strategies for resource optimization and carbon reduction in high-density urban environments.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Internet of things in rural agricultural freight transportation. A case study of North Dakota State
abstract: Efficient movement of agricultural goods remains critical to economic stability and food supply chain resilience in rural areas. However, traditional logistics systems in rural regions such as North Dakota face persistent challenges such as lack of real-time visibility, flexibility, and responsiveness. These lead to delays, increased costs, and post-harvest losses. Though, Internet of Things (IoT) offers transformative opportunities to enhance these agricultural freight systems, its integration into existing systems remains uneven and underexplored. This study conducts a comprehensive literature review of 60 peer-reviewed articles selected from an initial pool of 730 records to evaluate IoT applications, maturity levels, and implementation barriers in rural freight systems. The findings reveal substantial disparities in connectivity, data integration, sustainability alignment, and policy readiness, particularly in under-digitized rural environments. To address these gaps, the study proposes a six-layer IoT adoption framework tailored to rural agricultural freight transportation. This framework integrates technological, organizational, and policy dimensions to support scalable and context-sensitive implementation. This paper concludes by outlining measurable performance indicators and strategic priorities for policymakers and industry stakeholders seeking to advance resilient and sustainable IoT-enabled rural logistics systems.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Solving a rich vehicle routing problem with a heterogeneous fleet and trailers in medium-sized transport companies
abstract: Efficient route planning is a critical challenge for transport companies operating heterogeneous vehicle fleets. Manual planning often fails to leverage cost-saving consolidation opportunities, leading to suboptimal capacity utilization and increased operational costs. This paper addresses a real-world vehicle routing problem involving pickup and delivery tasks, heterogeneous vehicles and trailers, time windows, service equipment requirements, and labor constraints. We develop a matheuristic method that combines heuristic tour construction with exact optimization using a set partitioning model leveraging the manageable number of stops per tour.The proposed matheuristic is validated using real operational data from a medium-sized logistics provider based in Germany. Our experiments demonstrate that the matheuristic achieves average cost savings of 16.6% compared to historical plans, with solution times well under three minutes even for large instances. A comparison with a pure optimization model shows that while exact methods can yield marginally better solutions (up to 2–3% improvement), they are computationally impractical for real-time use. The matheuristic strikes a practical balance between solution quality and runtime, enabling automated, scalable, and cost-efficient routing for medium-sized transport companies with a heterogeneous fleet.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Learning-based emergency egress trajectory planning for UAV in mixed terminal airspace
abstract: Advanced air mobility (AAM) is expected to introduce increasingly heterogeneous low-altitude operations, and mature AAM deployment may create locally high-density traffic around capacity-constrained vertiports. This paper considers mixed operational scenarios in which unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft share the same vertiport and surrounding terminal airspace. In such environments, eVTOL operations typically follow air traffic management (ATM) procedures and are strategically deconflicted in advance, resulting in schedules that are largely inflexible. By contrast, certain UAV missions, such as time-critical medical deliveries following intercity eVTOL transport, require immediate departure and cannot wait for global replanning. Safely allowing emergency UAVs to egress from locally dense or capacity-constrained terminal airspace without disrupting pre-planned eVTOL operations therefore poses significant operational challenges. To address this problem, we develop an Asynchronous Proximal Policy Optimization (APPO) based reinforcement learning approach for emergency UAV egress that explicitly encodes separation safety and egress efficiency. A distributed policy-training framework based on Ray RLlib is developed, and the simulation environment incorporates the AirLib flight-control model from AirSim to represent low-level UAV maneuver responses during speed and heading command execution. Simulation results demonstrate that, under locally dense terminal traffic conditions, the proposed approach demonstrates stronger overall robustness than APF, VO, RRT, Modified CL-RRT, and MCTS-UCT in terms of safe-egress performance, separation maintenance, and online computational efficiency.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Adaptive air traffic management via large language model augmented reinforcement learning
abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) presents a transformative approach to urban transportation by enabling safe and rapid air travel. However, ensuring safety remains a critical prerequisite for large-scale deployment. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has demonstrated promise as a tactical deconfliction method, offering real-time speed advisories to maintain safe separation between aircraft. Yet, the manual design of reward functions and hyperparameter tuning is time-consuming and often lacks adaptability across varying scenarios. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an LLM-augmented MARL framework that uses LLMs to generate candidate reward-weight configurations offline and then selects among pre-trained MARL policies according to user preferences and system-level performance metrics. Rather than performing online reward reshaping during execution, the proposed framework improves adaptability by decoupling reward-parameter exploration from preference-conditioned policy recommendation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using LLMs to reduce manual reward tuning effort and support human-preference-aware tactical deconfliction under diverse operational priorities.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Data-driven UAV network design for emergency medical services under spatio-temporal uncertainty
abstract: Designing reliable Unmanned Aerial Vehicle networks for Emergency Medical Services is fundamentally challenged by the profound multi-dimensional uncertainty of demand. Existing approaches typically rely on static coverage or steady-state queueing models with fixed average arrival rates, often failing to capture the complex interplay between intra-day fluctuations, inter-day stochasticity, and dynamic spatial shifts. To address this, we propose a novel data-driven two-stage distributionally robust optimization framework under Wasserstein ambiguity sets. Unlike traditional methods, we model the demand arrival rate profile itself as a random variable, thereby endogenously characterizing how temporal volatility induces spatial uncertainty. We formulate the problem by integrating facility location and capacity dimensioning with a queueing system to ensure response reliability. To tackle the resulting computational intractability caused by nonlinear critical traffic intensity constraints, we derive an exact linearization and reformulate the problem into a mixed-integer linear program. We further develop an Accelerated Mixed-integer Benders Decomposition algorithm, enhanced by valid inequalities via Sample Average Approximation, robust warm starts, and Reformulation-Linearization Technique cuts. Extensive numerical experiments using real-world data demonstrate that our proposed algorithm reduces computational time by orders of magnitude compared to standard decomposition methods. Furthermore, out-of-sample analyses reveal that our model significantly outperforms traditional queueing-based benchmarks, effectively mitigating tail risks and ensuring operational resilience in data-sparse and data-rich regimes alike.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: A predict-then-optimize framework for Just-In-Time arrival of vessels with probabilistic berth-availability forecasts
abstract: Just-In-Time (JIT) arrival is a state-of-the-art operational strategy that aligns inbound vessel arrivals with berth availability to reduce fuel consumption and anchorage waiting without sacrificing service reliability. However, while ship operators could adjust the inbound vessel’s arrival time through en-route speed planning, target-berth availability remains an exogenous and uncertain port-side factor. To address this coordination problem, this study develops a predict-then-optimize framework that probabilistically models berth availability and evaluates the value of probabilistic forecasts for en-route speed planning in a scenario-based JIT planning setting. First, in the forecasting stage, berth availability is proxied by the remaining time to departure (RTD) of the vessel currently scheduled ahead at the target berth. This quantity is predicted probabilistically using conformalized quantile regression with gradient boosting. Then, in the speed-planning stage, the resulting predictive distribution is incorporated into a risk-aware speed-planning model that captures the asymmetric operational consequences of early and late arrivals. Based on 5,418 vessel-reported estimated time of departure (ETD) records for container vessels at the Port of Hong Kong in 2025, the forecasting results demonstrate that the proposed method materially improves predictive accuracy relative to vessel-reported ETD and provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates for an operational use. Computational experiments further show that speed-planning decisions based on the full predictive distribution achieve lower and more robust cost outcomes than those based solely on vessel-reported ETD or on a single predicted departure time, with these advantages becoming more pronounced when late arrival may cause severe downstream disruptions.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Rail-to-city emergency supply operations for protective accessibility: Evidence from conflict-affected Kharkiv
abstract: Urban logistics in high-intensity emergencies, where armed conflict represents an extreme case, faces disruption that threatens timely and equitable access to essential goods. Conventional supply chain models optimise cost and efficiency, yet crisis response must also protect recipients by limiting exposure during access trips. This study develops a rail-to-city decision-support model that integrates rail backbone corridors with alternative last-mile channels under security constraints and operationalises protective accessibility as a threshold service standard (within 15 min vs over 15 min). Using Kharkiv (Ukraine) as a case, we construct a city-scale digital network (street topology, geocoded service points, and demand zones) and evaluate six feasible configurations combining alternative sets of rail stations (adaptive micro-hubs) with last-mile channels (volunteer couriers, postal/CEP service points, pickup points, and lockers). For each configuration, we estimate transport work (pk·km), route distance and time, the population share within the 15-minute threshold, and equity indicators for vulnerable groups. Results show that activating additional rail gateways yields an approximately linear reduction in total delivery distance (∼35,000 km per added station) and substantially expands ≤ 15-minute coverage; a hybrid rail–postal configuration improves protective coverage by up to 40 % relative to volunteer-only delivery. The findings provide implementable guidance on gateway activation, service-point densification, and actor-burden allocation to improve protective accessibility and resilience in protracted urban emergencies.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: FedGNN-SFCP: Federated graph neural networks for ship fuel consumption prediction with heterogeneous data fusion and missing data imputation
abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based ship fuel consumption prediction (SFCP) methods have attracted considerable attention from scholars in recent years due to their robust feature extraction capabilities. However, these methods highly depend on the quantity and quality of ship fuel consumption data. In practice, individual ships generate at most 365 noon reports per year, and privacy concerns prevent data sharing across companies, leading to data scarcity. Additionally, noon reports suffer from coarse daily granularity and missing values, compromising data quality. When ML-based SFCP models are trained on datasets with poor data quantity and quality, their performance degrades dramatically. To address these issues, we propose a novel federated learning (FL)-based method combining graph neural networks (GNN) and generative adversarial networks (GAN) for SFCP, named FedGNN-SFCP. First, to enhance data quality, we propose a GAN-based imputation method for handling missing data in ship noon reports and automatic identification system (AIS) data. Meanwhile, to address the low data granularity of noon reports, we leverage high-frequency AIS data, which provides hundreds of records per day. Specifically, we propose a novel multiple-layer heterogeneous graph construction method and employ a heterogeneous graph transformer to effectively fuse these heterogeneous data sources, thereby improving prediction performance. Second, to enhance data quantity, we introduce FL to SFCP tasks to enable collaborative training, allowing the model to learn from more data while preserving privacy. Furthermore, we propose adaptive federated proximal to address the challenge of training on heterogeneous data feature distributions from different ships. To evaluate FedGNN-SFCP, we conduct a series of experiments on three real-world ship fuel consumption datasets. The proposed FedGNN-SFCP achieves relative reductions of at least 7.21%, 9.63%, and 4.15% in root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error, respectively, compared to baseline methods. This demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of FedGNN-SFCP as a privacy-preserving solution under different data missing rates for SFCP in the maritime industry.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Two-phase truck-van-drone collaborative transportation with transshipment: a two-stage heuristic approach enhanced with reinforcement learning
abstract: Urban terminal transportation connects port-based freight flows with urban customers and plays a critical role in the efficiency and sustainability of city logistics systems. Rapid growth in e-commerce and increasing urban density have made such systems more complex, especially when freight must pass through intermediate warehouses and be delivered under heterogeneous accessibility constraints. However, most existing studies on ground-air collaborative delivery focus on simplified urban settings and do not fully capture warehouse transshipment operations or building-level delivery restrictions. This paper studies a truck-van-drone collaborative transportation problem with transshipment (TVDCTP-T), in which shipments are transported between ports and customers via transshipment at warehouses based on coordinated operations of trucks, vans, and drones. High-floor customer requests must be served by drones due to access limitations, whereas low-floor requests can be served by either vans (via couriers) or drones. Flexible docking is also allowed, enabling drones to land on vans different from their launch platforms. To support decision-making in large-scale terminal transportation systems, we develop a reinforcement learning enhanced cascade-based adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm. The solution approach jointly updates van routes and drone sub-routes when customer assignments change, allowing efficient exploration of tightly coupled ground-air decisions. Extensive computational experiments are conducted on both randomly generated instances and realistic cases based on urban logistics operations in Shenzhen. The results show that the proposed approach consistently outperforms benchmark methods in terms of total cost and computational efficiency, particularly for medium- and large-scale instances. Sensitivity analyses further reveal how request composition, high-floor demand ratio, drone fleet configuration, and time-window tightness influence system performance, providing practical insights for the planning and management of urban terminal transportation systems.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Two-echelon robot-assisted electric vehicle routing problem with pickup stations
abstract: Parcel distribution is the costliest, most time-consuming, and most emissions-sensitive leg of e-commerce’s last-mile logistics. We study a multimodal system that pairs robot-assisted delivery with self-pickup. The problem is motivated by an emerging integrated planning architecture in dense urban and campus settings, where Electric Vehicles (EVs) replenish local service points, while the last mile is completed by sidewalk robots and Pickup Stations (PSs). We formalize this setting as the Two-Echelon Robot-Assisted EV Routing Problem with PSs and Service Designations (2E-REVRP-PSSD). We propose a compact Mixed-Integer Linear Programming model and a two-stage matheuristic, coupled with a size-aware Simulated Annealing Adaptive Neighborhood Search and a two-index EV routing optimizer. Across small- to large-scale benchmarks, the matheuristic delivers strong solution quality, robustness, and scalability: it matches best-known solutions on small instances in seconds; on medium- and large-scale instances, it outperforms a two-hour Gurobi run on average and returns feasible plans for all cases within minutes. We also applied our proposed method to related benchmark instances and obtained 9 new best-known solutions, which are reported in the literature. Sensitivity and scenario analyses yield actionable guidance: depot-biased or demand-centered siting reduces first-echelon miles; discrete thresholds in capacity/range and pickup-station coverage unlock stepwise consolidations; EV choices dominate CO 2 reductions; and Pareto frontiers expose inexpensive gains in battery-risk margins but steep costs for extreme pickup convenience. The framework is directly applicable to dense urban neighborhoods, campus districts, and retailer-locker networks where EVs feed robot hubs and pickup stations, enabling low-carbon, customer-aware last-mile logistics.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: The three-dimensional bin packing problem with variable box size
abstract: Most research on Three-dimensional Bin Packing Problem (3DBPP) treats box size as fixed throughout the packing process. However, in practical packing scenarios, boxes containing garments, bedding items, or plastic foam materials are deformable, exhibiting both compressibility and extensibility. To better capture this reality, we introduce the Three-dimensional Bin Packing Problem with Variable Box Sizes (3DBPP-VBS), which allows changing box sizes during packing. We formulate the problem as a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model and develop a beam search-based algorithm (BSA) for its solution. While Gurobi can obtain optimal solutions for small-scale instances, BSA efficiently generates high-quality near-optimal solutions for larger instances within practical computational times. Extensive experimental results on the Martello and BR instances demonstrate that allowing box size variation significantly enhances space utilization, with improvements of 6.06% in small-size Martello instances and 1.22% in large-size BR instances. Our findings highlight the potential value of considering variable box sizes for improving the efficiency of the 3DBPP, particularly in small-scale scenarios such as packaging operations for express delivery and e-commerce companies.

title: Editorial: Web 3.0 and Metaverse technologies in logistics and supply chain management

title: CSR-driven strategic interactions between blockchain adoption and greenwashing in the platform supply chain
abstract: The credibility of corporate social responsibility (CSR)-driven initiatives has become a critical challenge in platform supply chains, particularly when third-party sellers may engage in greenwashing, and retailers must decide whether to adopt blockchain technology (BT) to verify CSR authenticity and safeguard credibility. This study develops a game-theoretic model to examine how the seller’s greenwashing incentives and platform participation interact with the retailer’s CSR engagement and BT adoption. The results show that the seller is more likely to adopt an adventurous (greenwashing) strategy when regulatory penalties are weak and market conditions favor opportunistic behavior, although BT changes these incentives by enhancing CSR verifiability. Such opportunistic behavior creates negative externalities for the retailer by undermining CSR credibility and reducing profitability. In response, the retailer’s CSR efforts follow a pattern: (a) tolerance at low penalty levels, (b) defense at moderate levels, and (c) inattention at high levels. Furthermore, the retailer’s decision to adopt BT depends on implementation cost and consumer skepticism, which implies that BT adoption is economically contingent rather than universally optimal. Adoption is particularly likely when the implementation cost is either extremely low or extremely high, as long as consumer skepticism remains moderate. Moreover, platform entry provides a viable alternative to greenwashing for the seller when affiliation enhances product valuation, which changes strategic payoffs and encourages the retailer to adjust contractual or participation terms. These findings highlight a fundamental trade-off between technology-based verification and incentive-based coordination, which indicates that BT is most effective when integrated into broader governance mechanisms to sustain platform trust and performance.

title: Corrigendum to “A two-stage Stackelberg game based at-stop departure timing and trajectory optimization for connected and automated bus in mixed traffic” [Transp. Res. Part E 212 (2026) 104952]
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Interactive Bi-LSTM: A novel approach for multi-channel vessel traffic flow prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of vessel traffic flow (VTF) is essential for enhancing maritime safety and improving the efficiency of cargo transportation and port operations. In multi-channel waterways, VTF exhibits strong temporal variability, pronounced fluctuations, and complex inter-channel correlations, which pose significant challenges for reliable forecasting. Existing deep learning methods often fail to effectively capture the dynamic interaction effects among channels, as well as the coupled spatiotemporal dependencies inherent in VTF data, leading to suboptimal prediction accuracy and stability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Multi-Objective Interactive Deep Learning Network (MOIDLNet) based on the Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) architecture. The proposed model introduces a novel hidden-state interaction mechanism that enables dynamic information exchange across channels within a unified temporal modeling framework, thereby effectively capturing inter-channel dependencies and their evolving patterns. In addition, a hybrid loss function, termed MSEDTW, is developed by integrating Mean Squared Error (MSE) with Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), allowing the model to jointly optimize point-wise accuracy and global temporal consistency. Extensive experiments are conducted on real-world AIS datasets collected from the Chengshan Jiao Promontory (CJP) and Caofeidian Port (CFDP). Sensitivity analyses on key hyperparameters, including iteration number, learning rate, and input sequence length, are performed to determine optimal model configurations. The experimental results demonstrate that MOIDLNet consistently outperforms conventional machine learning methods and representative deep learning models in terms of prediction accuracy and stability. These findings highlight the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach and its potential for supporting intelligent maritime traffic management.

title: Editorial: Web 3.0 and Metaverse technologies in logistics and supply chain management

title: Optimizing urban electric vehicle charging and battery swapping infrastructure: A location-inventory-grid model
abstract: The rapid rise of electric vehicles (EVs) places unprecedented stress on both urban mobility systems and low-voltage power grids. Designing battery swapping and charging networks that are cost-efficient, grid-compatible, and sustainable is therefore a pressing yet complex challenge: service providers must jointly optimize station locations, battery inventory, and grid interaction under high-dimensional uncertainty. We develop an integrated location-inventory-grid model and employ a continuous approximation approach to overcome the intractability of discrete formulations. Our analysis compares centralized versus decentralized charging, with and without participation in frequency regulation. The results reveal that centralized charging, when combined with frequency regulation, not only reduces cost but also strengthens grid stability. However, it may constrain operational flexibility near the optimum, potentially challenging efforts to mitigate environmental impacts by lowering battery inventories. These results offer actionable guidance for cost-efficient, environmentally sustainable, and grid-compatible scaling of urban EV infrastructure to meet the demands of large-scale EV adoption.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: A Benders and column generation method to the integrated airline schedule and aircraft recovery with gate reassignment
abstract: Disruptions are inevitable during airline operations, and disruptions cost airlines and the traveling public. Disruption recovery decisions are often made in a sequential process that includes flight rescheduling, aircraft rerouting, crew reassignment, passenger re-accommodation, and gate reassignment for airline operations. Such a sequential recovery approach alleviates the complexity of the whole recovery process but often causes further disruptions to airport gate assignments and high recovery costs for airlines and passengers. This paper presents a novel airline disruption recovery approach by integrating the schedule and aircraft recovery with gate reassignment. We propose a Benders and column generation (BCG) method to solve the integrated problem. By exploiting the favorable structure arising from the Benders decomposition framework, we provide two acceleration techniques for Benders subproblems, a separation technique and an effective infeasibility certificate, to enhance the efficiency of the BCG method. The proposed model is tested on real-world data. In our experiments, all test instances are solved by the BCG method under a five-minute threshold with optimality gaps within 5%. Compared with the sequential recovery approach, the integrated recovery approach significantly saves recovery costs and avoids infeasible gate reassignments caused by the sequential recovery approach.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Ride-sourcing services with user protection regulation of the cryptocurrency fare-reward scheme
abstract: The cryptocurrency-based reward scheme has emerged as an innovative incentive mechanism in ride-sourcing markets. By offering crypto-rewards whose value fluctuates over time, ride-sourcing platforms aim to attract more users. However, in practice, users require transparent information to make informed decisions on whether and how to use the rewards regarding their time-varying value. Often, the platforms intentionally obfuscate the value information in favor of their economic interests, rendering the true value of cryptocurrency-based reward opaque to users. Consequently, the use of this strategic obfuscation can lead to welfare losses for users as they may fail to achieve optimal benefits from crypto-reward redemption. Motivated by the welfare implication, this study investigates the impacts of the platform’s information obfuscation on market performance and user welfare, specifically under varying regulatory protective measures designed to mitigate information asymmetry. The regulatory approach limits the obfuscation effect to safeguard users’ welfare during reward redemption. This study considers two user segments based on their level of awareness: “savvy” users, who possess sophisticated knowledge of market dynamics and hold informed beliefs regarding future reward values, and “naïve” users, who lack such understanding and rely on limited information. Given these two types of users, this study analyzes the platform’s incentives to employ information obfuscation in pursuit of profit maximization. Subsequently, we extend our analysis to evaluate the efficacy of regulatory interventions. To quantify these impacts, we employ an agent-based simulation model that simulates market-driven fluctuations in crypto-reward values.This model captures the longitudinal interplay between reward valuation, user redemption behavior, and resultant welfare outcomes.Our findings offer critical insights for policymakers regarding regulatory enforcement and provide strategic guidance for platforms on optimal pricing and incentive design.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Optimal design of flexible bus service integrated with trunk transit under demand uncertainty
abstract: This paper develops a two-stage stochastic optimization framework for designing flexible bus service integrated with trunk transit under uncertain spatial demand. The proposed system jointly supports direct door-to-door service, flexible-to-trunk transfers, and flexible-to-flexible transfers. Passenger willingness to transfer (WTT) is modeled as a demand-partition mechanism, allowing both fixed and service-quality-dependent transfer preferences. To address the strong NP-hardness of the second-stage passenger assignment problem, we develop a reliability-based decomposition method with a tailored trip assignment heuristic for large-scale instances. Numerical experiments based on a Hong Kong case study show that the integrated design reduces total system cost by up to 19.0% relative to a conventional feeder-only flexible-bus-trunk system and by 5.1% relative to a flexible-bus system with ad hoc service. The model also quantifies the value of passenger transfer flexibility, showing that full willingness to transfer can reduce composite system cost by 10.0%. Overall, the results demonstrate the value of jointly coordinating flexible bus deployment, trunk transit integration, and passenger transfer behavior when planning multimodal transit systems under demand uncertainty.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: First-party and third-party complementary apps: investment in research and development, launching, and merger and acquisition
abstract: With the enormous growth of app usage and smartphone penetration, an increasing number of third-party developers are offering apps that are complementary to the top-leading core apps, aiming to target the massive audiences of these apps and to enhance the user’s experience. At the same time, top-leading developers may launch their own complementary apps that compete with the third-party apps in terms of quality. The impact of the third-party developer on the first-party developer is twofold: on the one hand, the former creates added value for the core app, which translates into additional profit for the first-party developer. On the other hand, the competition between the first- and third-party substitutable apps calls into question the benefit of launching the first-party substitutable app. At the same time, the third-party developer relies upon the large market of the core app, while his own market share may be eroded due to the competition between the two substitutable apps. In this study, we develop a game-theoretical model of a market consisting of three apps: a core app and two partially substitutable apps that both complement the core app. We investigate the R&D strategies of the developers and derive the conditions under which they choose to launch their complementary apps. In addition, we analyze the M&A strategy of the core-app developer. Several counterintuitive results emerge from the analysis, such as: (i) competition between the two complementary apps can be mutually beneficial; and (ii) a reduction in the quality of the first-party complementary app may, paradoxically, lead to an increase in its demand.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Capturing heterogeneous alternative acceptance in route choice behavior using stated choice experiments: a soft truncated choice approach
abstract: Acknowledging that cognitive limitations often prevent travelers from thoroughly evaluating all available route alternatives in complex travel choice situations, this study explores the significance of heterogeneous alternative acceptance in route choice behavior. To address this, Soft Truncated Choice Model (SfTCM) is introduced, along with the derivation of policy indicators to enable a better understanding of the impact of attributes on choice probabilities and market shares. Furthermore, the model’s flexibility and applicability are enhanced through extensions that incorporate heterogeneity and enable incremental model specification by deriving analytical expressions. A carefully designed stated choice experiment on route choice was conducted, systematically varying the number of available alternative routes across different choice sets to assess the heterogeneous impact of choice set size on alternative acceptance. Results demonstrate that individuals do not consistently evaluate all alternatives, as their decisions are influenced by socio-demographics, travel experience, and the number of alternatives presented. The proposed SfTCM consistently outperforms traditional models (MNL and Mixed Logit), offering a more realistic framework for understanding travel decision-making under cognitive constraints. This underscores that choice models assuming full alternative consideration may lead to biased forecasts and suboptimal policy recommendations in transportation; therefore, SfTCM provides a more accurate approach to capture heterogeneous route acceptance for improved travel behavior analysis and transportation policy-making in complex choice situations.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Hybrid electric platform supply vessel routing with speed optimization: Pathways to cost-effective emission reduction
abstract: Hybrid diesel-electric propulsion systems offer promising pathways to emission reduction in offshore supply operations, yet their adoption introduces complex operational challenges requiring integrated optimization of route planning, speed selection, charging strategies, and power allocation. This study introduces the Hybrid Electric Platform Supply Vessel Routing Problem with Speed Optimization and develops two alternative mixed-integer linear programming formulations, based on a time-space network and a discrete-speed model, respectively, that simultaneously optimize these interdependent decisions under fuel quota constraints for a platform supply vessel (PSV). While the discrete-speed model is computationally more efficient, the time-space network provides a more flexible foundation for future extensions to weather-dependent operational planning. Using realistic instances from operations in the North Sea, we benchmark hybrid PSV performance against two diesel-only references representing current industry practices: fixed design-speed operations and speed-optimized operations. Results demonstrate that operators currently using fixed speeds can achieve substantial emission reductions while simultaneously reducing total costs through combined hybrid propulsion and speed optimization. For operators already employing speed optimization, hybrid PSV operations can achieve moderate emission targets with stable abatement costs of approximately 0.77 NOK/kg CO2 (67 EUR/ton CO2). Our analysis further quantifies the critical role of operational factors in determining the cost-effectiveness of hybrid operations: offshore wind farms prove essential for achieving ambitious emission targets by eliminating costly detours to remote charging stations, while voyage time budget flexibility creates favorable trade-offs between operational efficiency and emission reduction costs. These findings offer actionable insights for maritime operators navigating the transition to hybrid propulsion systems under increasingly stringent environmental regulations.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Collective adoption challenges in maritime digital platforms: a multi-stakeholder perspective
abstract: Digital platforms are widely promoted for improving coordination, visibility, and data exchange in maritime logistics. Yet many platform initiatives struggle to achieve sustained and widespread engagement in practice. This study explains why digital platforms struggle to achieve collective adoption among multiple stakeholders involved in maritime logistics, including different tiers of freight forwarders, shippers, and manufacturers. Using a qualitative research design, this study identifies a cascade of misfits between platform design assumptions and the institutional and operational structures of the industry. These misfits propagate at the platform design, collective adoption, and organizational implementation levels, ultimately leading to fragmented and selective platform use. The findings reveal that adoption is constrained not simply by technological limitations but by systemic misalignments across actors, roles, workflows, and governance arrangements. This study contributes to the logistics and supply chain literature by explaining why digital platforms fail to scale in asset-intensive environments and by identifying the conditions, such as shared standards, interoperability, and cross-actor alignment, that are needed to enable meaningful digital transformation in maritime logistics.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Joint information design and pricing for transportation information service
abstract: This paper analyzes how a Transportation Information Service (TIS) provider can leverage information design and its associated information service pricing as joint strategic tools to manage traffic congestion. We develop a Bayesian persuasion model for a two-route network with uncertain affine congestion costs, where the provider aims to either minimize the expected total social cost (e.g., a public authority) or maximize profit (e.g., a commercial firm). We compare two fundamental information policies: a common-information policy, which broadcasts the same signal to all subscribers, and a personalized-information policy, which sends private route recommendations. Our results show that providing full information for free is not optimal. Instead, the social-cost-minimizing strategy involves providing full information at a positive price to travelers. Under the assumptions of our model, this strategy also maximizes provider profit, creating an alignment of incentives between a social planner and a commercial entity. Furthermore, while personalized information is superior for congestion mitigation and can achieve the first-best system optimum under certain conditions, we prove a strong profit-equivalence result: the maximum profit achievable under personalized information is identical to that under the simpler common-information policy. Consequently, a profit-seeking provider does not need to invest in complex personalization solely for revenue gains.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Cross-border e-commerce platform strategy design and analysis: Reselling versus agency
abstract: Considering a cross-border e-commerce (CBEC) market involving multiple players of a CBEC platform, the supplier, and consumers, where the CBEC platform integrates the cross-border logistics services to connect the supplier and consumers. To investigate whether the CBEC platform can effectively promote the CBEC service, we deploy the game-theoretic approach to establish two business models without and with the CBEC platform. The model with the CBEC platform is designed by two channel strategies, namely, the reselling strategy and the agency strategy. The platform in the reselling strategy acts as a reseller and procures products from the supplier, while the platform in the agency strategy serves as a third-party entity to benefit the supplier for self-stores. Equilibrium results concerning the CBEC platform’s profit, the supplier’s profit, and consumer surplus can be derived from the two models. The merits of integrating CBEC services can be obtained by comparing the results of the two models. Results show that the model with the CBEC platform outperforms the model without the platform in terms of promoting the supplier’s profit and consumer surplus. Findings regarding which channel strategy should be implemented for the CBEC platform can also be obtained, where the reselling strategy should be chosen when the commission rate is low while the agency strategy should be chosen otherwise. Further findings show that several factors, e.g., the tax tariff, the investment cost coefficient, and the service level coefficient, will also affect the final results. Managerial implications regarding promoting CBEC platform operations are proposed and discussed lastly, including customizing CBEC channel strategies for targeted markets/regions, increasing the commission rate, and enhancing the CBEC platform’s services.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Online task assignment in warehouse considering the pickers’ dynamic capability: A data-driven optimization approach
abstract: Dynamic variations in pickers’ capability are crucial for task assignment efficiency, yet are often overlooked in research due to the focus on system-level optimization and the complexity of modeling human variability. This paper addresses the problem of order fulfillment task assignment considering the pickers’ dynamic capability. A unique feature of the proposed approach is the integration of a data-driven model for characterizing capability with a mixed integer programming optimization model for online task assignment. To solve the model and leverage the pickers’ dynamic capability, we developed a variable time window algorithm based on the proportion of available pickers. Numerical experiments are conducted using data obtained from a warehouse located in Southwest China. The results indicate that our approach significantly improves the accuracy of characterizing pickers’ capability. Additionally, our model modestly reduces total execution time and achieves a notable improvement of over 20% in labor equilibrium. With the help of our model, the warehouse manager can clearly assess the dynamic variations of pickers’ capability and make informed task assignment decisions, ensuring efficient and equitable labor utilization.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Regulating crowdsourced delivery under urban congestion: The role of order consolidation
abstract: Order consolidation in on-demand delivery services presents a critical trade-off among logistical efficiency, customer satisfaction, and urban congestion. This paper investigates the strategic decisions of stakeholders in this system and evaluates regulatory policies designed to mitigate market distortions and negative externalities. To do so, we develop a game-theoretic equilibrium framework of a two-sided delivery market that endogenizes both order consolidation and traffic congestion. Our analysis reveals that while a social planner operates at zero profit in an uncongested market, positive profits can be socially optimal once congestion externalities are accounted for. We identify a conditional consolidation-regime condition, evaluated at a given operating scale, based on two competing forces: the marginal congestion externality and the platform’s courier fleet-supply cost pressure. This condition determines whether the platform under- or over-consolidates relative to the social benchmark at that operating scale. We show that a single policy may be ineffective at steering the platform toward the first-best outcome. A commission cap paired with a physical bundling constraint is effective. We further extend the model to capture network capacity degradation from curbside parking friction. This extension shows how curbside friction affects the marginal traffic externality of delivery activity and can shift the consolidation regime.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Beyond the next port: A multi-task transformer for forecasting future voyage segment durations
abstract: Accurate forecasts of segment-level sailing durations are fundamental to enhancing maritime schedule reliability and optimizing long-term port operations. However, conventional estimated time of arrival (ETA) models are primarily designed for the immediate next port of call and rely heavily on real-time automatic identification system (AIS) data, which is inherently unavailable for future voyage segments. To address this gap, the study reformulates future-port ETA prediction as a segment-level time-series forecasting problem. We develop a transformer-based architecture that integrates historical sailing durations, destination port congestion proxies, and static vessel descriptors. The proposed framework employs a causally masked attention mechanism to capture long-range temporal dependencies and a multi-task learning head to jointly predict segment sailing durations and port congestion states, leveraging shared latent signals to mitigate high uncertainty. Evaluation on a real-world global dataset from 2021 demonstrates the proposed model consistently outperforms a comprehensive suite of competitive baselines. The result shows a relative reduction of 4.70% in mean absolute error (MAE), 4.95% in mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and 2.59% in root mean squared error (RMSE) compared with sequential deep learning models. The relative reductions compared with gradient boosting machines are 7.03% in MAE, 39.49% in MAPE and 4.37% in RMSE. The case study conducted on one major destination port further illustrates the model's superior accuracy.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Distributionally robust assortment and inventory optimization with ship-from-store for omnichannel retailers
abstract: Ship-from-store (SFS) has become a prominent initiative for modern retailers to implement an omnichannel strategy. Despite its significant benefits, SFS complicates the coordination of assortment and inventory, which is crucial to enhance the profitability while maintaining the service level. This challenge is aggravated by endogenous complex customer choices across channels and products. To address this challenge, we consider an omnichannel retailer (o-tailer) operating a set of physical stores and relying on SFS to fulfill online demand, and study joint assortment and inventory optimization with SFS over a multi-period sales horizon. We develop separate multinomial logit models for distinct-channel customers to characterize their heterogeneous choice behaviors. Based on partial moment information of market share distributions, we formulate a nonlinear distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model that incorporates customer channel migration. We propose a tractable solution framework that synergistically integrates linearization technique, DRO reformulation, enhanced linear decision rule, and Benders decomposition algorithm, which complement each other to efficiently overcome the computational intractability. The results of extensive numerical experiments suggest that the proposed framework consistently yields high-quality solutions and significantly outperforms several benchmark approaches. We perform sensitivity analyses to investigate the impacts of key parameters on the o-tailer’s financial and operational performance metrics. We further quantity the benefits of implementing distinct store assortments and the SFS program. Some beneficial technical and managerial insights are derived from the empirical findings.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Promoting green port-hinterland transportation: A branch-and-price algorithm for electric truck charging management
abstract: Electric trucks are increasingly deployed for port-hinterland cargo transportation to reduce diesel dependency, yet their charging activities have an important impact on energy costs, transportation efficiency, and grid security. Current research has not yet fully addressed charging management problems that simultaneously account for these multi-dimensional factors. To address the above challenge, this study proposes a novel mixed-integer programming model by considering time-of-use tariffs, demand charge tariffs, and departure delays for charging electric trucks, aiming to minimize time-of-use energy costs, demand charges to reduce peak power demand, and penalty costs associated with departure delays. Then, we reformulate the problem as a set-covering model, and develop a column generation approach to obtain high-quality solutions efficiently. Furthermore, we propose a branch-and-price algorithm to derive the optimal solutions within the reasonable solving time. Numerical experiments on real-world cases are performed to verify the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed solution algorithm. We explore the impacts of the charging power, unit demand charge and unit penalty cost to provide valuable references for managing charging activities of electric trucks within port-hinterland transport systems.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Robust home healthcare routing problem and resource assignment considering robot collaboration and service disruptions: A hybrid Benders and column generation method
abstract: Home healthcare involves medical and caregiving services for patients at home. Coordinating a multi-skilled workforce and managing consumable and non-consumable resources pose challenges. Poor service quality can lead to disruptions, necessitating rework in service delivery. To address these issues, we propose a two-echelon home healthcare routing problem considering personnel collaboration and service disruptions. The first echelon involves a routing problem with multi-skilled workers and resource allocation. The home healthcare center and vehicles have capacity limits for transporting workers and resources. New technologies, such as care robots, assist caregivers and reduce service times. Since services may face disruptions, an additional routing problem is formulated to handle reworking services in the second echelon. On the other hand, service quality, travel time, and service time are influenced by randomness and box uncertainties. To deal with this, we propose a robust stochastic-box programming, solved through a combination of genetic algorithm (GA), column generation (CG), and Benders decomposition (BD). GA is used as the initial solution for CG, while BD is applied to solve the subproblem of CG. The proposed method is evaluated by solving 50 instances, with the results demonstrating its superiority. To assess robustness, the deviation coefficient and uncertainty level are increased in a case study, leading to reduced risk. Finally, three managerial sensitivity analyses showed that enhancing worker skill scores improved service quality, increasing absences raised service completion time, and replacing vehicles with lower-cost drivers decreased the objective function by 15%.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Make waves: quantifying the impact of the Red Sea crisis on global container port turnaround time
abstract: The Red Sea crisis, a major maritime disruption event, has attracted widespread attention. This crisis disrupted global shipping networks, increased voyage distances, and caused delayed cargo deliveries. As critical nodes in maritime transport, ports may experience operational disruptions from typical maritime events. While anecdotal evidence suggests substantial port-level effects, rigorous empirical evidence remains limited. To address this gap, this study utilises global Automatic Identification System (AIS) data to calculate port turnaround time (PTT) for the top 100 container ports. Then, we apply Difference-in-Differences (DID) and Regression Discontinuity Design-Difference-in-Differences (RDD-DID) models to capture the sustained average effect and immediate impact of the crisis on PTT. Both methods isolate seasonal and cyclical influences during the observation period. Our analysis shows that the crisis increased ports’ PTT in both models, with results that satisfy the parallel trends assumption as validated through event study methodology. Employing the same testing procedures combining DID, RDD-DID, and event study approaches, we further identify the route-based regions affected by the Red Sea crisis. The results indicate that the impacts varied across regions. For the affected regions, we also conduct heterogeneity analyses which reveal significant immediate and sustained PTT escalations across large ports and ports with automated terminal. Further analysis of the PTT sub-metrics reveals that berthing operation time (BOT) experienced both immediate and sustained increases, whereas waiting for berth time (WBT) exhibited only a significant sustained increase following the Red Sea crisis. This study provides evidence that crises at critical maritime chokepoints can propagate to the port sector. These findings provide valuable insights for shipping companies and ports, enabling them to proactively mitigate the negative impacts of such disruptions and to enhance their responsiveness and flexibility when confronting similar crises in the future.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Scheduling passenger and freight co-modal transport for a high-speed rail reservation platform: a column-and-row generation-based modular framework
abstract: High-speed rail (HSR) corridors operating at high frequencies within urban agglomerations often exhibit uneven temporal distribution of passenger volume and imbalanced passenger flows along train trajectories, creating opportunities to expand freight services. To leverage the capacity, we redesign the off-peak ticketing mechanism into a time-slot-based HSR reservation (TRS) platform, through which both passengers and carriers reserve travel sections and receive exact departure times after scheduling. The problem is formulated as a two-layer decision model that integrates line planning and scheduling: the first decision level aligns reservation demand with train stop patterns, while the second decision level refines detailed schedules by accounting for differences in train speeds and priorities. A column-and-row generation–based framework decomposes the problem into modular “carriage-train-schedule” components, dynamically generating candidate carriages and violated constraints to approximate feasible train routes. Numerical experiments across 47 scenarios on both a small-scale corridor and the Yangtze River Delta HSR network show that the proposed algorithm solves five-station instances using only 9.7% of the CPU time required by the Gurobi solver. It also efficiently handles large-scale 37-station network cases involving over 38,065 passenger trips and 2,907 tons of freight in total. Furthermore, under a “weak” passenger-priority principle, TRS enables efficient co-modal transport by increasing operating revenue by 4.88% and passenger seat utilization by 13.05%, while delay penalties account for less than 1% of total revenue. At the same time, operating multi-mode trains during off-peak periods does not result in severe network congestion.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Editorial Board
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Model-assisted multi-agent reinforcement learning for collaborative synchromodal transport re-planning under service time uncertainty
abstract: Synchromodal transport operations frequently require rapid re-planning in response to uncertain terminal service times, yet such decisions are typically made by multiple carriers with heterogeneous objectives and decentralized control. This study investigates collaborative re-planning in synchromodal transport networks under service-time uncertainty from a multi-carrier perspective. We formulate the problem as a decentralized decision-making process in which carriers must coordinate re-planning actions while preserving individual rationality. To address this challenge, we propose a model-assisted multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework that combines heuristic plan generation with learning-based carrier coordination. An adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) heuristic is used to generate feasible candidate re-planning options, while carriers are modeled as learning agents that decide whether to accept or reject these options through a consensus mechanism. Rather than directly optimizing a centralized model, carriers learn acceptance policies based on local observations and realized outcomes, without requiring prior knowledge of service-time distributions. An event-triggered and regret-based learning scheme is introduced to align global delay mitigation with carrier-specific cost preferences under uncertainty. Extensive computational experiments on a realistic synchromodal transport network demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves re-planning performance compared with benchmark strategies. The results show that decentralized, heterogeneous multi-agent coordination can outperform centralized and homogeneous approaches, particularly in scenarios with high uncertainty and avoidable delays. Mechanism and ablation analyses further reveal the structural importance of multi-agent decomposition, carrier heterogeneity, and the temporal allocation of decision preferences along the transport chain. Additional analyses examine sensitivity to key reward hyperparameters and negotiation round limits, robustness under alternative disruption distributions and network-graph perturbations, and controlled extension settings with more carriers and transshipments. The proposed approach provides a practical decision-support methodology for collaborative synchromodal transport re-planning under uncertainty.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Delayed matching strategies in demand-responsive transit: The role of market thickness
abstract: Tidal demand in cross-regional travel can cause peak-period shortages and off-peak underutilization in fixed-route transit. Although Demand-Responsive Transit (DRT) offers greater flexibility, its performance depends critically on when requests are matched and how delayed matching is coordinated with passenger pooling and meeting points (MPs). We formulate this problem as an event-driven Semi-Markov Decision Process that accounts for stochastic request arrivals and heterogeneous expected pickup times (EPTs). In pairwise settings, we show that the optimal delayed-matching policy follows a threshold structure determined by the time remaining until a passenger’s EPT and the required pickup travel time. We then develop the Dynamic Threshold and Market Thickness (DTMT) strategy for pooled services and further integrate it with spatiotemporal MP clustering to obtain MP-DTMT. Numerical experiments and a case study based on MTA Line 646 show that DTMT consistently outperforms Greedy and Batching benchmarks, while MP-DTMT further reduces total cost by 37.8%–46.1%. The results reveal how market thickness increases the value of waiting, whereas MP coordination preserves temporal flexibility by reducing pickup travel requirements. This study provides interpretable dynamic-matching strategies for DRT systems facing volatile tidal demand.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Dynamic pricing optimization for waste recycling networks: a spatiotemporal incentive framework
abstract: The global plastic waste crisis demands innovative recycling solutions that are both economically viable and operationally efficient. Traditional recycling networks, often relying on uniform pricing and decentralized decision-making, frequently suffer from spatial imbalances, facility congestion, and prohibitive collection costs. This paper tackles these challenges by introducing a spatiotemporal dynamic pricing framework designed for plastic waste recycling, utilizing existing retail gas stations as decentralized collection hubs. Unlike conventional models that address pricing, facility location, and route in isolation, the proposed approach co-optimizes these decisions within a unified model under explicit capacity and regulatory constraints. A pivotal innovation involves the development of a consumer choice model that explicitly captures the trade-off between financial incentives and travel distance – a behavioral nuance often oversimplified in prior literature. The resulting complex optimization problem is reformulated into a computationally tractable mixed-integer linear program through a linearization technique. The framework’s efficacy is rigorously validated via extensive numerical experiments and a large-scale case study centered on Houston’s Loop 610 corridor. Results demonstrate that the proposed location-based pricing strategy yields a statistically significant enhancement in net profitability and achieves a 46.3% reduction in collection costs compared to a conventional uniform pricing strategy, while simultaneously ensuring regulatory compliance and mitigating localized congestion. This research provides an actionable and scalable decision-support tool, underscoring that the integrated optimization of incentives and logistics via existing infrastructure is instrumental for improving recycling performance, reducing operational expenditures, and advancing the transition toward a circular economy for plastics.
