title: A unified deep reinforcement learning framework for solving the heterogeneous fleet vehicle routing problem
abstract: The Heterogeneous Fleet Vehicle Routing Problem (HFVRP) incorporates diverse vehicle capacities, fixed costs, and variable travel costs, making routing decisions highly sensitive to vehicle selection. Most existing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods assume homogeneous fleets, leading to suboptimal performance when applied to HFVRP. To address this, we investigate HFVRP under complex constraints and develop a unified DRL framework capable of solving the problem across diverse settings. We formulate a Mode-Switching Markov Decision Process, modeling the generation of HFVRP solutions as a single-stage autoregressive decision process. Accordingly, we propose a Mode-Switching Cross-Semantic Multi-View framework (MS-CSMV), a unified architecture featuring a cross-semantic encoder and a multi-view decoder that effectively addresses diverse problem constraints and captures the complex mapping relationships between vehicle heterogeneity and customer node attributes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MS-CSMV significantly outperforms state-of-the-art neural solvers and achieves a favorable balance between solution quality and computational efficiency, producing solutions within seconds. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robust zero-shot generalization capabilities across large-scale instances and previously unseen problem variants.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Real-time yard slot allocation for outbound containers in an automated container terminal based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Efficient yard slot allocation for outbound containers is paramount to enhancing ship loading efficiency in automated container terminals (ACTs), where the perpendicular yard layout and the twin yard crane (YC) configuration are widely deployed. In such ACTs, the storage of an arrived outbound container relies on a twin-YC relay process where the container is initially stacked in a temporary handshake slot by the landside YC and subsequently remarshalled to a seaside slot by the seaside YC, presenting a complex relay-type yard slot allocation problem (RYSAP). This problem essentially comprises two decision-making processes: Decision 1 allocates a handshake slot for an arrived outbound container, while Decision 2 selects an outbound container from the handshake area and allocates a seaside slot for it. Structurally, each decision-making process is decomposed into two hierarchical stages: Stage 1 constructs a stack-set to bound the decision space for Stage 2, and Stage 2 determines the specific slot within the stack-set. To cope with the uncertainties in container arrivals and decision triggering, this problem is addressed in real time via a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based method. For Stage 1, the stack-set selection strategy is designed to construct the stack-set at each decision-making point. For Stage 2, a DRL method is proposed for specific slot allocation, aiming to reduce the number of blocking containers and enhance space utilization. By integrating the two interconnected decision-making processes, a comprehensive Markov Decision Process (MDP) is formulated. Crucially, the mathematical expectation of the number of future blocking containers at the current state is incorporated into the reward function, thereby guiding the DRL agent to learn a forward-looking policy. To accelerate training convergence and enhance policy performance, a Double Dueling Deep Q-Network with effective random exploration (D3QN-ERE) is developed. Numerical experiments verify the effectiveness, stability, and favorable generalization capability of the proposed method. Further analysis of the experimental results provides some suggestions for improving the yard operation and management.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Data-driven robust optimization for emergency facility deployment under ambiguous demand position
abstract: Under the uncertainty of disaster locations, the deployment of emergency facilities is a core challenge, which directly determines the efficiency of emergency response and thereby reduces the time required to deliver emergency services. To address the spatial uncertainty of future demand points, we propose a cluster-wise Wasserstein distance-based spatial ambiguity set via historical demand clustering to characterize future demand distribution. We first formulate a distributionally robust optimization model for locating emergency facilities from the perspective of minimizing the transport distance. Then from the target-oriented decision-making perspective, we propose a cluster-wise robust satisficing model to maximize the robustness to the uncertainty of achieving a specified satisfactory target transport distance. A solution technique based on row-and-column generation is proposed to tackle the large-scale discrete models efficiently. We conduct numerical experiments to verify the validity of the discretization method in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy under the proposed algorithm. The results show that the robust satisficing model has better average performance than the benchmark models. Finally, the robust satisficing framework is applied to deal with a real case of locating emergency facilities in Sichuan, an earthquake-prone region of China.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: A robust optimization approach for the urban last-mile network of high-speed rail logistics integrating drone delivery
abstract: As a sustainable and efficient freight transport method, high-speed rail (HSR) logistics is developing rapidly. However, its potential is limited by the inefficiency and uncertainty of urban last-mile delivery. This paper proposes a two-stage robust optimization model for designing an urban last-mile delivery network of HSR logistics that integrates drone delivery. This paper focuses on the practical scenarios the model jointly optimizes the activation modes of logistics functions at HSR stations, the location selection of urban distribution centers, and their hierarchical affiliation relationships, while considering factors such as differentiated facility construction modes, drone flight range, and no-fly zones. To solve the model efficiently, an improved column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm is developed, and acceleration strategies such as scenario reduction are introduced. Numerical experiments based on real-world data from Shenzhen City, China show that the improved C&CG algorithm outperforms the Benders decomposition algorithm and the basic C&CG algorithm in terms of the number of iterations and computation time. Additionally, the two-stage model demonstrates better cost efficiency and demand satisfaction rate than the single-stage robust model in an uncertain environment. Sensitivity analysis further reveals the trade-off relationships among drone delivery costs, network robustness, and facility investment. This study can provide an efficient decision-making method for the layout optimization of urban delivery networks in HSR logistics.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Distributionally robust UAV fleet deployment for traffic network monitoring under state-dependent demand uncertainty
abstract: Effective traffic network monitoring is fundamental to intelligent transportation systems, enabling congestion management, incident detection, and emergency response. While unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer flexible alternatives to fixed infrastructure, their deployment faces significant uncertainty from fluctuating traffic demand and volatile environmental conditions. This paper addresses the strategic UAV fleet deployment problem under joint demand and environmental uncertainty through a novel two-stage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) framework with state-dependent ambiguity sets and an observability-dependent support-width mechanism. We develop a fixed-siting dual analysis and finite-support computational model that capture how UAV siting changes a bounded proxy for the modeled width of the demand support; the mechanism does not assert that siting causally changes physical traffic demand. Our model extends classical facility location formulations by incorporating empirical Wasserstein ambiguity sets with two-sided mean bounds and compact, siting-dependent supports conditioned on observable operating states, allowing robust decisions without requiring complete distributional knowledge. We derive exact recourse and samplewise transport duals for fixed siting and an exact linear-programming oracle for an explicitly declared finite support. The computational study uses one recomputed Shanghai-context synthetic benchmark in which all visited configurations are evaluated by the finite-support model. A canonical output ledger, independent primal–dual checks, ambiguity-constraint audits, nested support refinement, and repeated common-path evaluation make the numerical evidence internally traceable. The results remain scenario-specific and do not establish field calibration, universal dominance of DRO, or causal effects of siting on realized demand.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Planning urban air mobility network with travel mode choice under uncertainty
abstract: This study investigates an urban air mobility (UAM) network planning problem that incorporates passenger travel mode choice through a trip inconvenience cost framework. Under an expected-cost minimization objective, the model jointly determines vertiport deployment, airway activation, and passenger mode choice based on trip inconvenience costs, while explicitly accounting for two sources of uncertainty. Under demand uncertainty, passenger mode preferences are explicitly embedded into the system design model. A key theoretical result shows that the stochastic demand formulation is equivalent to its deterministic expected-value counterpart. The study further considers travel cost uncertainty and formulates a corresponding two-stage stochastic program, for which the above equivalence no longer holds. Instead, the stochastic model is transformed into a deterministic approximation via sample average approximation (SAA). To solve the two resulting stochastic models efficiently, the enhanced benders decomposition algorithm is developed based on a dualization-based reformulation. To further improve computational efficiency, several acceleration techniques are introduced, including stabilization strategy, a difference-based trip reduction, and a zone-based demand aggregation. Numerical experiments on the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area dataset demonstrate the advantages of the proposed formulations and the effectiveness of the solution approach. The results also yield actionable managerial insights and provide practical guidance for UAM network design.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Co-opetition game analysis of the third-party logistics firm and recycling platform considering consumer inertia
abstract: To investigate how consumer inertia influences the service level and recycling-market encroachment strategy of a third-party logistics firm (3PL), we develop and compare two game-theoretical models: the Platform-only recycling scenario and the Both-party recycling scenario in which the 3PL encroaches on the recycling market. Our results show that, compared with the Platform-only recycling scenario, the 3PL generally has an incentive to strategically reduce the service-level offered to the online recycling platform after encroachment. Further extension analyses show that this service-degradation result is relatively robust. Even when the 3PL loses its second-mover response advantage, faces penalty constraints for service degradation, or when the online recycling platform has an information advantage regarding the proportion of inertial consumers, the tendency toward service degradation generally remains. However, under certain conditions, the 3PL may also have an incentive to improve the service-level offered to the online recycling platform. In addition, we find that the 3PL does not necessarily provide a higher service-level in its self-operated recycling channel. When consumer inertia level is high, the 3PL instead tends to provide a higher service-level to the online recycling platform than to its self-operated recycling channel. Moreover, 3PL encroachment does not always hurt the online recycling platform, and a higher consumer inertia level does not necessarily protect the platform’s profit. For the 3PL, a low consumer inertia level facilitates its entry into the recycling market, whereas whether a high consumer inertia level deters encroachment depends on the match between the encroachment benefit and the entry cost. The extended analyses further confirm the robustness of this finding and yield several new insights. Under the penalty constraint mechanism, an increase in the minimum service-level requirement discourages 3PL encroachment, whereas a higher unit penalty cost may expand the feasible region for encroachment. Under information asymmetry regarding the proportion of inertial consumers, if the true proportion of inertial consumers in the market is low, an increase in consumer inertia level may instead enlarge the feasible encroachment region of the 3PL. Moreover, under certain conditions, 3PL encroachment can generate a win–win outcome for both the online recycling platform and the 3PL. This outcome is jointly affected by the unit cost coefficient of service-level, consumer preference for the 3PL’s online recycling channel, unit recycling revenue, and consumer inertia level.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: A digital Multi-Layer waterway modeling framework for constrained port waters
abstract: In constrained port waters, vessel navigation is jointly influenced by channel geometry, traffic regulations, and operational constraints, leading to complex and heterogeneous vessel movement patterns that cannot be adequately characterized by conventional waterway modeling methods. To fill in this research gap, this study, therefore, proposes a digital multi-layer waterway modeling framework by leveraging Automatic Identification System (AIS) data with chart-based information, including three layers: navigable space layer, waterway zoning layer, and behavioral analysis layer. The navigable space layer first identifies dominant navigation patterns using an adaptive clustering algorithm based on trajectory similarity. Representative boundaries are reconstructed to approximate the effective navigable space implied by vessel movements. Next, waterway zoning layer performs semantic matching between trajectory point clouds within the identified navigable space and chart-based waterway geometries. A maximum connected component strategy is employed to refine and filter trajectory points that are semantically aligned with each waterway, while residual outliers are further clustered to examine potential emerging waterways. Based on these results, updated waterway boundary representations are derived. Finally, behavioral analysis layer investigates vessel movements within the semantically annotated waterway by combining spatiotemporal feature analysis with multivariate statistical testing, enabling quantitative assessment of behavioral variability across different waterways. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a case study in the Ningbo-Zhoushan Port, where updated semantic boundaries increased point-weighted AIS coverage from 0.870 to 0.994. Behavioral analysis further shows a statistically significant but moderate association between waterway and vessel maneuvering behavior, suggesting the value of jointly encoding geographic structure, semantic attributes, and navigation behavior in digital waterway maps.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Assessing the dynamic robustness of higher-order multi-modal public transit network considering passenger preference choices
abstract: Public transit networks (PTNs) should be sufficiently robust to absorb shocks and reduce the negative impacts of failures. Although previous studies have made progress in evaluating the dynamic robustness of PTNs, they have commonly overlooked passenger preference choices in dynamic redistribution of failed passenger flow (DRFPF) and higher-order interactions between stations, particularly for multi-modal PTNs (MPTNs). This paper models failures in a higher-order directed MPTN to better understand the impact of failures in one system (e.g., rail transit) on other systems (e.g., bus and taxi/ride-hailing). Specifically, we organize the MPTN with group interactions into simplicial complexes, propose a simplicial load-capacity model, and devise a DRFPF approach that accounts for passenger preference choices and origin–destination demands. The weighted directed MPTN covers three conventional public transit modes, bus, rail, and taxi/ride-hailing, and complements the connections with public bike and walk. Finally, taking the Beijing MPTN as a case study, we evaluate its dynamic robustness under attack scenarios using multi-scale metrics and further conduct sensitivity analyses. The results show that even under the same attack strength and origin station, different destination demands of sudden heavy passenger flow can lead to significant variations in cascading failures of the MPTN. Furthermore, the introduction of higher-order simplicial failure propagation not only enlarges the scale of the eventual collapse but also causes failure propagation to exhibit more pronounced characteristics of regional diffusion, intensified fluctuations, and risk convergence. This study can be valuable to transport engineers and planners working toward building robust public transit systems.
keywords: Dynamic redistribution of failed passenger flow
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Route-aware detection of ship collision avoidance manoeuvres via change point analysis with intention inference
abstract: Reliable and human-consistent collision avoidance is essential for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) operating in mixed traffic environments. A key challenge is the extraction of representative critical encounter scenarios from real-world data without relying on predefined risk thresholds or expert-driven rules. This study proposes a data-driven, route-aware framework for detecting ship collision avoidance behaviours and extracting the critical encounter scenarios in which such behaviours occur. The framework comprises three components. First, ship motion patterns are analysed to characterise normal route-following behaviour, enabling collision avoidance behaviour to be distinguished from routine navigation. Second, a unified cost function is formulated to jointly evaluate multiple kinematic features while explicitly incorporating planned route information, enabling separation of route-following course changes from potential avoidance actions. Change Point Detection (CPD) method is then applied to identify behavioural transitions and segment ship trajectories into candidate collision avoidance manoeuvres. Third, an intention-informed encounter identification approach is introduced, where avoidance intent is inferred by comparing observed trajectories with virtual route-following trajectories. This enables confirmation of true collision avoidance behaviour and extraction of the associated critical encounter scenarios. The proposed method is validated using Automatic Identification System (AIS) data from the high-traffic Øresund region, including the Helsingør-Helsingborg ferry corridor. Results on a labelled dataset show strong performance, achieving an F1-score of 0.8203 and 0.7443 in behaviour identification and encounter extraction, respectively. The findings demonstrate that the framework can robustly identify avoidance manoeuvres and capture critical encounters. Moreover, the proposed behaviour identification method is further applied in various navigational environments to verify its generalisation. The proposed critical encounter extraction framework provides empirically grounded insights into MASS development and testing, maritime situational awareness enhancement, and traffic management.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Examining impacts of tradable credit schemes on delivery services using an agent- and activity-based simulation framework
abstract: This paper presents a generalized Tradable Credit Scheme (TCS) framework for urban logistics. We rigorously compare an integrated market (MoLoCo), where urban mobility and last-mile delivery activities share a unified currency (Coins), against a sector-specific market (LoCo) with an independent emission cap for logistics. This study explores the regulatory effectiveness of these frameworks and evaluates the efficacy of adaptive operational strategies employed by a monopoly logistics provider. Using an agent- and activity-based simulation for Munich, Germany, we evaluate regulatory effectiveness and adaptive logistics strategies. Results indicate that MoLoCo framework benefits from a “Coupling Effect,” where the mode shift to low-emission travel modes stabilizes the Coin market prices, yet this triggers a “Green Logistics Paradox” by stimulating online shopping. Conversely, LoCo framework generates high Coin market prices that force decarbonization but risk a “Reverse Modal Shift,” driving cost-sensitive users back to physical stores and worsening congestion. Regarding logistics strategies, fleet electrification is cost-effective but fails to mitigate congestion. True spatial efficiency is achieved only through cargo bikes in the dense city center. We therefore propose a sequential TCS implementation roadmap: initiate sector-specific regulation to enforce technological adoption, then transition to an integrated market to maximize societal welfare.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Global maritime logistics resilience amid trade conflicts: forecasting port risk and identifying critical roles via spatiotemporal graph neural networks
abstract: The escalation of trade conflicts since 2018, compounded by geopolitical disruptions including the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia–Ukraine conflict, and the Red Sea crisis, has placed unprecedented strain on global maritime logistics. Using a spatiotemporal graph neural network framework and AIS data from January 2019 to December 2024, this study aims to forecast port operational risk and identify critical port roles in risk propagation. We construct monthly shipping networks for four vessel types, namely container ships, bulk carriers, general cargo ships, and oil tankers, and synthesize a composite risk index from standardized in-port time and waiting time. The selected ST-GNN models outperform both the LSTM and ARIMA baselines, while the neighborhood dependency analysis provides further evidence that network information contributes additional predictive value. Model-extrinsic counterfactual analysis quantifies three port role dimensions, namely Source, Sink, and Mediator, representing risk emission, risk absorption, and network bridging, respectively, and identifies differentiated role profiles and high-intensity transmission links. Results reveal that the most active ports in risk propagation are predominantly small and medium-sized specialized ports, and that the strongest transmission follows direct Source-to-Sink connections. Risk propagation patterns differ across vessel categories and are consistent with differences in their network structures and underlying shipping and trade patterns during a period characterized by sustained disruptions.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Drivers of public engagement in social media discourse on self-driving vehicles: psychological and emotional determinants
abstract: Research on self-driving vehicles (SDVs) has largely overlooked the influence of framing strategies on public interests and public engagement on social media discourse regarding SDVs. We address this gap by analysing 102,174 Twitter posts to examine how emotional sentiment and psychological distance shape engagement across private, public, and commercial SDV contexts. Grounded in Construal Level Theory and Appraisal Theory of Emotion, we identify thematic and emotional drivers of interaction. By leveraging large-scale social media analysis, this study advances understanding of the cognitive and emotional mechanisms underlying SDV discourse, offering insights for more effective public communication and consumer engagement strategies. Our analyses show that psychologically proximal topics (e.g., safety or pricing) elicit stronger engagement in private vehicle discourse due to personal relevance. Further, high-arousal negative emotions (fear, anger) spark immediate, intense responses, while low-arousal positive emotions (happiness) encourage sustained, reflective engagement.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Stochastic two-echelon vehicle routing with mobile satellites: Adaptive large neighborhood search with stochastic approximation scheduling
abstract: This paper studies the stochastic multi-commodity multi-depot two-echelon vehicle routing problem with mobile satellites (3M-2E-SVRP), where first-echelon vehicles serve as mobile transfer points for second-echelon deliveries under synchronization and time-window constraints. Travel and service times are modeled as independent truncated log-normal random variables in controlled stochastic benchmark instances. To solve the problem, we develop SAS-ALNS, an adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm that integrates deterministic approximation scheduling with stochastic approximation scheduling to evaluate feasibility, reliability, and expected failure costs during the search. Two stochastic planning perspectives are considered: a penalty-based model (PBM), which minimizes deterministic routing cost plus expected failed-delivery penalties, and a chance-constrained model (CCM), which imposes minimum customer-level on-time service probabilities under the modeled uncertainty. Computational experiments show that deterministic planning substantially underestimates late-arrival risk: under stochastic evaluation, deterministic solutions incur high expected failure costs and leave 27.1% of customers below a 95% success-probability threshold. PBM and CCM reduce expected failure costs by approximately 96% while achieving average customer success probabilities above 99%. SAS closely matches Monte Carlo simulation for both central and upper-tail arrival-time statistics while requiring substantially less evaluation time. Representative in-search comparisons with simulation-based candidate evaluation further show that SAS provides a favorable balance between solution quality, reliability stability, and computational effort. The results show that distribution-based stochastic schedule evaluation can be embedded efficiently into ALNS and improve the reliability of synchronized mobile-satellite routing decisions within the controlled benchmark and independence assumptions considered.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: The incentive schemes of ride-hailing platforms for passengers with heterogeneous behaviors: Coupons or priority matching?
abstract: In the ride-hailing market, heterogeneous passenger behaviors during a ride lead to differences in whether they are willing to exert effort to maintain civilized behavior and obtain a high behavioral score, while passengers who do not exert effort may impose a loss on drivers. The platform operates a scoring system and decides whether and how to incentivize passengers to maintain high scores. To analyze this problem, we develop a game-theoretic framework involving three parties (the platform, passengers, and drivers) and compare three platform policies: no-incentive scheme, coupon incentive scheme, and priority matching scheme. The results show that without incentives, collective effort would improve outcomes for all participants. However, passengers have no individual incentive to exert effort, even when the platform sets a relaxed scoring standard, thus trapping the market in the civilization dilemma. This dilemma can be perfectly resolved by the coupon incentive scheme, consequently creating a civilized market with a “triple-win”. While the priority matching scheme only partially addresses the civilization dilemma, it outperforms the coupon incentive scheme in platform profitability when the platform sets a relaxed scoring standard. We further examine the dual-incentive schemes and observe that it yields lower platform profits than a single-incentive scheme. These results can guide platforms to optimize the ride-hailing operation environment and improve their profitability.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Subsidizing buyers or stage-stations? Platform subsidy strategies in community group buying
abstract: As an innovative e-commerce model, community group buying (CGB) has grown rapidly since the pandemic period, especially in developing countries. In CGB, a platform (serving as an e-tailer) selects nanostores as community stage-stations to provide consumers with services such as order notification, storage, and after-sales support. After orders are placed, goods are delivered to stage-stations, where consumers pick them up. Platform subsidies are widely used in e-commerce to encourage participation and expand markets. What distinguishes CGB is that, because buyers and stage-stations are interdependent, the platform can subsidize not only buyers (i.e., consumers) but also stage-stations to coordinate the market. We investigate the implications of subsidy strategies in both incremental (noncompetitive) and competitive markets using a stylized model. Our analysis shows that subsidies are not always profitable for the platform: The platform subsidizes buyers or stage-stations only when consumers’ basic valuation is sufficiently low. Conditional on subsidizing, stage-station subsidization becomes more attractive when the unit unfitness cost is low. Interestingly, buyers or stage-stations may benefit more from indirect rather than direct subsidies. By comparing incremental and competitive markets, we further show that the platform is more likely to prefer buyer-side subsidization in the competitive market. In particular, as competition intensifies, the platform can earn higher profit by adopting more flexible subsidy strategies, although social welfare may decrease. Our study provides important implications for how CGB platforms can use subsidy strategies to expand their markets and consolidate their positions.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Multi-level optimization for the deployment of battery swapping in inland waterways
abstract: Containerized battery swapping offers a promising pathway to zero-emission inland waterway transport. However, its deployment requires coordinated decisions among actors with conflicting objectives. We introduce a multi-level optimization model with three actors: a policymaker who allocates subsidies to maximize adoption, an infrastructure developer who selects station locations to maximize profit, and fleet operators who minimize operating costs. We formulate this as a multi-level optimization problem, reduce it to a bilevel program via Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions, and solve it using an iterative bilevel decomposition and a problem-specific large neighborhood search. Experiments on the Dutch–Belgian inland waterway corridor show that a market equilibrium cannot exist without public intervention, the optimal subsidy mix depends on the available budget, and that within an intermediate price range the minimum budget for full adoption remains stable. Sensitivity analyses on costs, battery range, and network size are reported together with an alternative emissions-reduction objective.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Multi-modal transportation network design integrating UAM mode: an activity capacity-based approach
abstract: With the rapid development of electric Vertical Take-off and Landing (eVTOL) technology, Urban Air Mobility (UAM) has emerged as a promising travel mode. However, its early development faces critical challenges, including the design of the low-altitude transportation network, which serves as essential infrastructure, and the need for seamless air-ground coordination due to a limited number of eVTOL airports and their restricted coverage, necessitating strategies like transportation capacity matching and timetable synchronization. Simultaneously, substantial growth in urban residents’ activity demands places immense pressure on transportation networks, potentially hindering urban vitality if not adequately addressed (e.g., residents forgoing additional activities due to congestion). Therefore, developing a multi-modal network design method that integrates UAM and tackles these pressing issues is increasingly urgent. While Traffic Network Capacity (TNC) is a commonly used optimization objective in network design, existing methods often fall short in areas such as analyzing activity-oriented travel demand, incorporating land-use information, and supporting design requirements from the activity perspective, such as maximizing the capacity to accommodate activity flow. To address these critical gaps, this paper introduces the concept of Activity Capacity (AC). This concept addresses two major challenges: integrating early-stage UAM and alleviating the negative impacts of traffic congestion on urban vitality. Building on this concept, we propose a novel Multi-modal Network Design Problem (AC-MNDP) model. Our model optimizes urban infrastructure to maximize its capability for accommodating activity flows and balancing activity-travel demand and flow distribution. This framework offers practical, quantitative insights for urban planners. The model is structured into a three-layer programming approach: the upper-level model considers network design under investment constraints, the middle-level model focuses on maximizing AC within land-use and activity structure constraints, and the lower-level model is a multi-modal activity-travel assignment model. A sensitivity analysis-based algorithm is developed to solve the AC-MNDP model. Numerical case studies validate the model’s ability to generate multi-modal network design schemes under varying investment constraints, comparing AC-based with TNC-based design methods, and offering insights from a sensitivity analysis of UAM travel costs and capacity thresholds, which are valuable for urban air-ground network planning.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Simulation-based Bayesian optimization for large-scale dynamic lane allocation
abstract: The current traffic research highly relies on Simulation-Based Optimization (SBO) to evaluate complex operational strategies. However, large-scale network problems often involve hundreds of control decisions that make the search space extremely high-dimensional and computationally prohibitive. This study develops an advanced Bayesian Optimization (BO) method for the large-scale SBO and applies it to solve the Dynamic Lane Allocation (DLA) problem, which grants ride-sharing vehicles conditional access to Dedicated Bus Lanes (DBLs) with allocation decisions varying across both location and time. As a result, the problem requires binary decisions across hundreds of space–time units, creating an extremely high-dimensional, combinatorial search space that existing optimization methods cannot handle efficiently. To address this challenge, we introduce a Grouped Automatic Relevance Determination (GARD) Hamming kernel that separates temporal and spatial relevance in the Gaussian Process (GP) surrogate, a dynamic group-aware dimension-reduction mechanism that identifies influential regions of the solution space, and a trust-region adaptation tailored to binary decisions to improve sampling efficiency. These components are combined with hybrid candidate generation and mixed batch sampling to enhance robustness under limited simulation budgets. The method is evaluated using a trip-based Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (MFD) multimodal simulator on both a controlled virtual grid and the large-scale Barcelona network. Results show that the proposed BO approach consistently converges faster, achieves higher solution quality, and maintains feasibility under strict bus-service constraints compared with metaheuristic methods. The framework also demonstrates stable performance across varied OD patterns and scalability to real-world city networks.On the large-scale Barcelona network, the proposed method achieves, on average, a 14.2% lower final objective and 2.16 × faster convergence than Large Neighborhood Search (LNS), as well as a 1.1% lower final objective and 1.52 × faster convergence than Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS). These findings highlight the potential of the proposed method to support efficient decision-making in large-scale, binary, network-level traffic optimization.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Coordinating the port-carrier supply chain: Optimal design of volume-commitment discount contracts
abstract: Ports operate as capacity-constrained service platforms that face substantial demand volatility and congestion risk from multiple heterogeneous carriers. In this context, effective contracts between ports and carriers can help mitigate the inefficiency. This study develops a contract-based coordination framework that enables risk sharing and efficiency improvement in port-carrier cargo transfer. Specifically, we focus on volume-commitment discount contracts, under which the port offers a price incentive in exchange for the carriers’ binding commitment to a specific cargo volume, enhancing resource planning and operational efficiency. We first demonstrate that simple volume-commitment discount contracts, while Pareto-improving compared to no contract, fail to achieve full coordination due to double marginalization. In a multi-carrier context, shared and congestible port resources further make the contract design problem nonseparable across carriers. To achieve coordination, we develop a coupled volume-commitment discount and shortage-subsidy contract that induces system-optimal commitments, mitigates congestion externalities, and flexibly allocates surplus among participants. Comparative statics show that carrier heterogeneity shapes differentiated contract design. In particular, a substitution effect is revealed: the port tends to offer deeper discounts to carriers with lower shortfall-settlement costs when commitments from other carriers are harder to secure. The port also offers stronger incentives to carriers with higher demand uncertainty to manage congestion-related risks. Moreover, our findings further suggest that differentiated incentive contracts are more valuable for congestion-vulnerable ports with high planning benefits.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Supply chain resilience to geopolitical risks: integrative insights and future research directions
abstract: Global supply chains are increasingly exposed to persistent geopolitical risks arising from trade restrictions, sanctions, armed conflicts, export controls, and strategic competition among nations. These risks challenge traditional assumptions underpinning globally integrated and efficiency-oriented supply chains and call for a broader understanding of supply chain resilience. This editorial paper synthesises findings of nine articles examining how organisations and supply chain networks respond and adapt to geopolitical risks. Three interrelated themes emerge: geopolitical risks and strategic responses; network, collaboration, and alliance-based resilience; and strategic capabilities and technology-enabled adaptation. Synthesising these insights, we conceptualise supply chain resilience to geopolitical risks as the capacity of firms and their supply chain networks to anticipate and absorb geopolitical disruptions, adapt to changing exposure, and strategically reconfigure relationships, resources, and network structures while maintaining viable business operations. Such resilience is multidimensional and contingent, arising from the interplay among strategic choices, collaborative relationships, technological and operational capabilities, resources, and network structures. Six future research frontiers are identified concerning dynamic and multilevel geopolitical risks, resilient network design, capability configurations, inter-organisational governance, strategic reconfiguration, and methodological advancement. Together, the findings advance a more integrated, dynamic, and configurational understanding of how firms and supply chain networks remain resilient under persistent geopolitical uncertainty.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Acquiring and managing additional railcars attached to passenger trains for freight on rail transit under demand uncertainty
abstract: When faced with freight surges, fossil-powered trucks often incur negative externalities such as traffic congestion and environmental pollution, along with prohibitive costs and land limitations linked to road infrastructure expansion. To address these concerns, under-exploited rail transit has emerged as a freight alternative over recent decades. This paper investigates an innovative logistics approach that attaches additional railcars to intercity passenger trains within an unsaturated rail network for flexible freight transshipment and long-distance transport. To launch this, decision-makers need to, at strategic level, acquire and assign additional railcars to rail stations, followed by tactical decisions on selecting trains for railcar attachment and generating space-time cycles repeated within planning horizon. These interwoven decisions are complicated by demand uncertainty due to a lack of adequate historical data or accurate forecasting methods appropriate for this emerging freight alternative. Based on a space-time network representation of associated operations and decisions, we construct a mixed integer model that can render the strategic and tactical decisions robust and hedge against demand uncertainty. Given computational difficulties, we decompose the monolithic formulation into manageable problems and devise a constraint-and-column-generation (CCG) algorithm. Numerical experiments conducted on real-world problem instances with diverse network dimensions and characteristics demonstrate the computational superiority of CCG; elucidate the value of robust solutions; validate the benefits of jointly optimized decisions; and offer managerial insights.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Achieving net-zero emissions in logistics and operations: The net zero plus framework
abstract: Today, achieving net zero in logistics and operations is a top agenda for almost all organizations. In this context, there is no doubt that enabling technologies are critical for facilitating decarbonization (e.g., emissions reduction, offset, and removal). Moreover, fulfilling the net-zero goal naturally requires the participation of all stakeholders, within and beyond the traditional supply chains. This paper aims to critically examine the relevant studies on net-zero emissions in the operations and logistics literature, with the focal points on different major stakeholders (e.g., non-governmental organizations, governments, investors, service providers, supply chains, and consumers) as well as the role of enabling technologies. We also examine several real-world practices implemented by prominent firms (such as Apple, Amazon, and Nike). Based on the findings of literature review and observed practices, we establish a novel “Net Zero Plus” framework, where we highlight the underexplored potential of enabling technologies as a key “plus” to help achieve net-zero emissions. We further develop several propositions. Finally, we identify several research-practice gaps and then establish a real-practice driven future research agenda.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Instant retail strategies for online order fulfillment under consumer time sensitivity
abstract: This study develops a game-theoretic framework to examine an instant retail strategy in which an online platform collaborates with a physical retailer to provide a buy-online-ship-from-store (BOSS) service. We analyze two scenarios—without instant sale and with instant sale—based on the platform’s self-sale format and the retailer’s normal sale format. For each introduction scenario, we discuss two sub-scenarios depending on whether the delivery timeliness of the platform sale dominates that of the normal sale. These two sub-scenarios are defined as platform-led delivery advantage and retailer-led delivery advantage. Consumers exhibit time-sensitivity in receiving their online orders. Our findings reveal that when consumers exhibit strong time sensitivity, the adoption of the instant sale enables both the platform and retailer to elevate retail prices. Meanwhile, in the platform-led delivery advantage case, implementing an instant sale reduces the prices of the platform’s and retailer’s respective self-operated sale formats when the instant sale’s shipping cost is low. Conversely, a high shipping cost for the introduced instant sale allows for those price increases. In this high-shipping-cost circumstance, competition among the three sales formats can be softened. The results also demonstrate that the instant sale benefits the platform and retailer when the instant sale’s delivery time and shipping cost are either sufficiently low or high enough. Notably, in the retailer-led delivery advantage case, the platform and retailer always benefit from the instant sale. For the retail system, introducing an instant sale format enhances consumer surplus and social welfare regardless of the delivery advantage. These findings remain robust under various extensions, including uniform price strategies, differential commission fee structures, and the incorporation of store sales.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Mesoscopic pedestrian dynamics enhancement robust optimization for signage collaboration in metro stations under uncertainties
abstract: Dynamic guidance signage in metro stations demonstrates significant potential for enhancing evacuation efficiency, primarily by proactively adapting to passenger flow distributions and the evolution of risk, thereby optimizing the overall evacuation route network. To address the uncertainty of fire risk, this paper proposes a dynamic guidance signage coordinated control method incorporating robust optimization. First, a cell transmission model is constructed to dynamically model the passenger evacuation process in metro stations, capturing the temporal evolution of passenger flows under fire conditions. Second, a budget uncertainty set is introduced to characterize fluctuations in fire risk, and the dynamic guidance signage optimization problem is formulated as a robust decision-making problem that seeks an optimal and stable coordinated guidance strategy under the worst-case realizations of uncertain parameters. Subsequently, a solution algorithm is developed by integrating a local search mechanism with a global optimization framework. Compared with conventional metaheuristic algorithms, the proposed approach exhibits significant advantages in both solution quality and convergence efficiency. Finally, extensive numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results indicate that, compared with static guidance strategies, the coordinated dynamic guidance signage strategy could significantly improve evacuation performance. In addition, the impacts of key factors, including robust parameters, weight configurations, solution algorithms, crowd density, fire scenarios, and signage adjustment frequency, on the dynamic guidance system performance are systematically analyzed.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Toward efficient urban regional mobility: a region-oriented optimization framework for high-capacity autonomous ride-sharing
abstract: High-capacity autonomous ride-sharing services have significant potential to improve urban mobility efficiency and enhance transportation accessibility, particularly in areas characterized by concentrated travel demand and homogeneous trip patterns. To advance the performance of high-capacity ride-sharing systems in such environments, this study proposes a region-oriented optimization framework that integrates mobility-driven regional partitioning, intra-regional high-capacity ride-sharing, and cross-regional vehicle coordination within a unified operational architecture. Real-world ride-hailing data are utilized to identify tightly connected mobility communities and translate them into operational regions for subsequent ride-sharing operations. Within each region, a path-set-based vehicle-passenger matching model is developed by integrating offline shareable-path-set generation with online vehicle-passenger matching. To address spatiotemporal demand fluctuations, cross-regional vehicle dispatching is further incorporated as a system-coordination mechanism for balancing vehicle resources across operational regions. Case studies based on New York City ride-hailing data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework under heterogeneous urban demand conditions. The identified operational regions effectively capture areas dominated by short-distance travel demand. Across regions with different demand densities, the proposed matching optimization model improves vehicle utilization and service accessibility while substantially reducing total vehicle mileage, with limited impacts on passenger waiting times and detour distances. In addition, the cross-regional dispatching strategy alleviates supply–demand imbalances and further enhances passenger service performance. This framework provides actionable insights for the design of high-capacity autonomous ride-sharing services and supports the transition toward more efficient and sustainable urban transportation systems.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: A sequential fix-and-optimize framework and pricing-guided search for efficient truck scheduling at a cross-docking terminal
abstract: Cross-docking facilities play a critical role in modern freight distribution systems by enabling rapid consolidation and redistribution of shipments with little or no intermediate storage. As cargo handling volumes continue to increase, inefficient coordination between inbound unloading, internal transshipment, and outbound loading operations often leads to severe congestion, prolonged truck waiting, and departure delays, significantly increasing operational costs. This paper addresses a cross-docking truck scheduling problem aimed at determining coordinated service plans that minimize total operational cost, including truck waiting, freight handling, temporary storage, and delay penalties under tightly coupled inbound-outbound interactions. An efficient mixed-integer linear programming model is developed together with two innovative solution frameworks designed to overcome the computational complexity of the decision problem. The first framework adopts a sequential fix-and-optimize strategy that progressively constructs a feasible service plan through precedence-consistent batching, thereby substantially reducing problem dimensionality while preserving global scheduling feasibility. The second framework introduces a pricing-guided search mechanism in which single-truck insertion pricing is exploited to systematically identify cost-reducing schedule modifications, allowing promising structural adjustments to be explored without repeatedly resolving the full optimization model. A comprehensive computational study demonstrates that the proposed formulation and solution frameworks consistently produce high-quality schedules with significantly improved computational efficiency across a wide range of problem instances, thereby providing an effective and scalable decision support tool for managing large-scale and congestion-sensitive cross-docking operations in modern freight distribution systems. Moreover, a series of sensitivity analyses is performed to gain strategic insights regarding the key tradeoffs during cross-docking operations.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: A large language model-empowered approach to trajectory prediction for edge deployment on ships
abstract: Large language models (LLM) are driving the deep integration of artificial intelligence and intelligent shipping, ushering in a new technological paradigm. Although existing deep learning–based ship trajectory prediction methods have achieved significant progress, their capacity to integrate non-numerical semantic knowledge remains insufficient, yet such knowledge is crucial for accurately characterizing ship behavior patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose LLM-EdgeSTP, the first LLM-empowered and edge-deployable ship trajectory prediction framework that unifies continuous automatic identification system (AIS) trajectories with discrete maritime textual knowledge through cross-modal reasoning. The method comprises three core components. (1) The maritime semantic prompt unit (MSPU) transforms raw AIS trajectories into context-aware natural language prompts. (2) The navigational interaction representation unit (NIRU) models ship–ship interactions by fusing convolutional and attention mechanisms and maps them into the LLM embedding space through representation–language reconstruction to enable semantic understanding of encounter and avoidance intentions. Lightweight LLMs such as LLaMA and Gemma then fuse navigational states and interaction semantics to generate trajectory predictions in natural language form and decode them into precise coordinates. (3) Edge deployment supports real-time inference on low-power hardware. Experiments across three representative maritime regions demonstrate that LLM-EdgeSTP outperforms ten baseline models by an average of 40% in terms of average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) while satisfying real-time latency requirements. This work lays a key technical foundation for building interpretable, efficient, and practical autonomous navigation systems.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: A Deep Reinforcement learning model for centralized route recommendation in multi-modal transit networks
abstract: Rapid urbanization has outpaced public transit infrastructure expansion, leading to severe peak-hour congestion in various metropolitan areas. While route recommendation systems offer a solution, conventional passenger-centric approaches typically optimize trips in isolation, neglecting aggregate network effects and causing inefficiencies resulting from “selfish routing”. To address this, we propose Temporal Perception Multi-head Proximal Policy Optimization (TP-MPPO), a centralized Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework designed to optimize multi-modal public transit networks holistically. Acting as a virtual Traffic Management Center (TMC), the framework monitors vehicle loads and station queues to generate coordinated routing strategies for clusters of passengers. Rather than enforcing mandatory route assignments, TP-MPPO adjusts the displayed ranking of route alternatives in passenger-facing menus. Conditional on the ranking–choice association captured by a calibrated route-choice model, this reordering is used in simulation to redistribute demand toward less congested multi-modal alternatives while preserving passengers’ freedom to choose. The architecture combines a group-specific multi-head self-attention mechanism to process heterogeneous passenger data, a transformer-based module to model evolving traffic dynamics, and a multi-head PPO policy for targeted recommendations. Evaluated through three independent full-day simulation runs of Beijing’s multi-modal transit network, TP-MPPO achieves the best mean performance among the evaluated benchmark methods, reducing average waiting time by 11.8%, average trip time by 6.7%, the top-five hexagonal congestion index by 28.5%, and waiting passengers by 12.3% relative to the strongest baseline for each metric.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Equitable and visually attractive arc routing for residential waste collection with heterogeneous fleets
abstract: The residential waste collection problem (RWCP) is an arc routing problem in which multiple vehicles must service street segments while adhering to capacity and working-time constraints, with the possibility of multiple visits to landfills. In practice, route plans should be not only cost-efficient but also equitable across vehicles and visually attractive. This study addresses a multi-vehicle RWCP with heterogeneous fleets, where vehicles may differ in capacity and driver efficiency, and where route costs incorporate turn penalties. We formulate the problem as a mixed capacitated arc routing problem with intermediate facilities, in which service requirements are defined on both arcs (directed street segments) and edges (undirected street segments), and propose a hierarchical graph-partitioning-based matheuristic (H-GPM) to solve it. The proposed framework decomposes the problem into three stages: vehicle-level balanced clustering, trip-level capacitated clustering, and trip-level routing. At the vehicle level, it combines graph coarsening, Steiner tree-based route-cost estimation, initial solution construction, and local improvement to generate workload-balanced and spatially coherent task assignments. At the trip level, vehicle-specific subgraphs are partitioned into capacity-feasible trips, and routing decisions are determined by lexicographic MILP models that first minimize arc overlap and subsequently route cost. Computational experiments show that, compared with baseline methods for homogeneous fleets, H-GPM produces workload-balanced solutions while substantially improving visual attractiveness, particularly by reducing spatial overlap among vehicle routes. For heterogeneous fleets, H-GPM effectively accounts for turn penalties, vehicle capacities, driver efficiencies, and multi-trip operations, producing feasible and workload-balanced solutions. The evaluation of the embedded route-cost estimation procedure further supports the reliability of the proposed framework.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Assortment planning with product customization capabilities in omni-channel retailing
abstract: Customers are increasingly seeking personalized products, making customization a critical consideration for retailers. At the same time, many retailers are shifting from single- or multi-channel strategies to an Omni-channel approach. So, this study aims to develop a model that assists Omni-channel retailers in incorporating customization into their assortment planning decisions, which has been neglected in previous research. To address the issue of customization in an Omni-channel retailer’s assortment planning, identifying the Point of Differentiation (POD) is emphasized as a key component in implementing a delayed differentiation strategy that facilitates product customization. To simulate customer decision-making behavior and demand within the Omni-channel environment, an exogenous demand model is employed, and a quadratic function is introduced to model retailer profit. The proposed model is reformulated as a Binary Integer Programming model, and a heuristic method is introduced to solve it. Using this heuristic, two policies of demand acceptance are introduced and compared, several analyses are conducted, and managerial recommendations are provided. The study concludes that offering customization can enhance retailers’ profits and reduce lost sales; however, high customization setup costs and demand uncertainty may offset these benefits.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Hazardous materials multimodal transport routing Problem: A robust optimization approach based on Benders decomposition
abstract: This paper develops a robust optimization framework for hazardous materials multimodal transportation under road congestion, carbon regulation, and uncertainty. Road impedance functions are used to characterize road congestion effects on travel time, carbon-emission cost, and transportation risk cost, and a budgeted box uncertainty set is introduced to capture operational uncertainty. Hazmat Scenario-Enhanced Adaptive Multi-Cut Benders Decomposition (HSA-MBD) algorithm is proposed to solve the resulting model efficiently. Experiments on the Shanghai network show that road congestion, carbon constraints, and uncertainty jointly affect route and mode choices. Road congestion shifts the optimal solution from road-intensive routes toward rail-waterway-based intermodal configurations and sharply reduces feasibility under severe conditions. Tighter carbon caps further encourage cleaner paths with lower road dependence, whereas across the tested deviation-ratio sensitivity ranges, uncertainty mainly amplifies total cost without changing the optimal path, although transportation-risk uncertainty can alter the route structure when it is introduced as the sole uncertainty source. For the Shanghai multimodal network, the hazardous-material shipment considered, and the tested uncertainty-budget and deviation-ratio ranges, transportation-risk uncertainty has a substantially stronger effect on total cost than freight-rate uncertainty. In addition, HSA-MBD obtains the same best-known objective values as the benchmark methods for all tested instances, while requiring fewer Benders iterations and less computational time.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Review of flow capturing, flow covering, and flow interception models
abstract: This paper was written to honor John Hodgson and his contributions to location science. Starting with the usual location-allocation models, we follow flow interception, (including flow covering and flow capturing) models from their inception to today’s versions. We then demonstrate how their formulations relate to the corresponding standard models. These modifications in conjunction with the known degree of difficulty of the standard models provide a glimpse into the hardness of the flow covering, capturing, and interception models. We propose a variety of modifications to the models investigated in the literature that can result in future research papers. Such future papers will extend the applicability of flow capturing, covering, and interception models.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Investigation of the reservation-based travel scheme for the morning commuting problem with heterogeneous commuters
abstract: Morning commuting has long been a critical challenge for urban transportation systems, characterized by a large volume of travel demand concentrated within a short time window. Motivated by recent reservation-based travel experiments in Beijing, this study aims to theoretically explore the reservation-based travel scheme and the corresponding commuter behaviours, accounting for heterogeneity in commuters’ willingness to make reservations. Under this scheme, commuters with permits are granted access to the designated reservation lanes, while those without permits must use the conventional lanes. The conditions for an effective reservation scheme that avoids capacity waste are given. It has been shown that, under an effective reservation scheme, the travel cost for commuters using the reservation lane decreases, while that of commuters in the non-reservation lane remains unchanged. The optimal number of reservation permits to minimize the total travel cost is derived. Compared to that without a reservation scheme, the total travel cost for all commuters is reduced by a factor proportional to the relative capacity of the reservation lane, scaled by one-fourth, under the optimal number of reservation permits. The reservation scheme is extended to a multi-period scheme, in which the peak period is divided into several subperiods, requiring commuters to select a specific subperiod when making reservations. It is demonstrated that the multi-period scheme is significantly more effective in reducing travel costs for commuters.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Price competition and inventory turnover along China’s new energy vehicle supply chain
abstract: Despite the rapid expansion of China’s new energy vehicle (NEV) market, inventory turnover among listed firms in the NEV supply chain has not improved consistently. This study examines how price-competition pressure is associated with days inventory outstanding (DIO), using lagged leave-one-out peer gross-margin compression as an accounting-based proxy. We develop a two-period model that connects product substitutability to equilibrium margin compression, derived demand, capacity-constrained inventory adjustment, and DIO. The predictions are tested using 2,426 firm-year observations for 390 Chinese A-share-listed firms from 2016 to 2024. A one-standard-deviation increase in peer gross-margin compression is associated with an approximately 3.0% increase in DIO, or 3.3 days at the sample mean. Cost of goods sold contracts substantially while average inventory changes little; their coefficient difference is 1.780 with a standard error of 0.276. The DIO response strengthens with customer concentration and is significantly larger for upstream and midstream firms than for downstream firms. Additional estimates reported in the Appendix link peer gross-margin compression to weaker profitability, higher inventory write-down provisioning, and longer accounts receivable days. The findings show that inventory turnover slows when operating activity adjusts faster than inventory, especially under greater customer dependence and derived-demand exposure.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: The rider-drone-locker routing problem in last-mile delivery
abstract: This paper studies the Rider-Drone-Locker Routing Problem (RDLRP), a last-mile delivery problem in which riders collect orders from merchants under ready-time constraints, and each order is served either directly by a rider or, after depot handover, by a drone delivering it to a customer-accessible locker. The problem jointly determines rider routes, service modes, locker and drone assignments, and ground-air synchronization. Order-level depot copies are introduced to represent intermediate handovers and allow riders to revisit the depot within a route without using trip-indexed variables. We formulate a mixed-integer programming (MIP) model and a branch-and-cut (BC) exact framework with root-node separation of rounded capacity connectivity and mode-dependent rounded cover inequalities, and implement a problem-tailored adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) algorithm incorporating ready-time scheduling, delay-aware insertion, penalized infeasible search, and elite-pool restart. Computational results show that the ALNS reproduces all proven optima on the smallest instances and consistently obtains high-quality feasible solutions for instances with up to 100 orders. The sensitivity analysis further provides managerial insights into the effects of drone resources, locker deployment, self-pickup compensation, and drone operating costs on system performance and service-mode decisions.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Two-stage stochastic optimization for maritime search and rescue with service guarantees
abstract: Maritime incidents can lead to severe casualties, environmental damage, and substantial economic losses, making rapid and reliable emergency response a core task for maritime authorities. In practice, planning for maritime search and rescue (MSAR) is challenging because incident occurrence is uncertain in time and location, and rescue demand varies across scenarios. This paper studies a two-stage MSAR planning problem that jointly optimizes pre-incident facility location and resource prepositioning decisions as well as post-incident service assignment decisions under uncertainty. The objective is to minimize the total preparedness cost of facility construction and resource prepositioning while satisfying prescribed service guarantee requirements at all incident sites. We formulate the problem as a two-stage stochastic integer programming model with service guarantee constraints, where the service guarantee level of an incident site is defined as the probability that its demand is fully satisfied in demand-positive scenarios. To solve the model, we transform it into a feasibility verification problem by specifying service guarantee targets and, drawing on Blackwell’s approachability theorem, derive a necessary-and-sufficient feasibility condition for a given facility-location and resource-prepositioning plan. Based on this result, we develop a two-stage solution framework for solving the problem efficiently. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method outperforms deterministic benchmarks in total cost and remains comparable to the sample average approximation (SAA) method, with a maximum total-cost gap not exceeding 0.13%, while requiring substantially less computation time.
journal_title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Constrained reinforcement learning for the dynamic inventory routing problem under stochastic supply and demand
abstract: Green hydrogen has multiple use cases and is produced from renewable energy, such as solar or wind energy. It can be stored in large quantities, decoupling renewable energy generation from its use, and is therefore considered essential for achieving a climate-neutral economy. The intermittency of renewable energy generation and the stochastic nature of demand are, however, challenging factors for the dynamic planning of hydrogen storage and transportation. This holds particularly in the early-adoption phase when hydrogen distribution occurs through vehicle-based networks. We therefore address the Dynamic Inventory Routing Problem (DIRP) under stochastic supply and demand with direct deliveries for the vehicle-based distribution of hydrogen. To solve this problem, we propose a Constrained Reinforcement Learning (CRL) framework that integrates constraints into the learning process and incorporates parameterized post-decision state value predictions. Additionally, we introduce Lookahead-based CRL (LCRL), which improves decision-making over a multi-period horizon to enhance short-term planning while maintaining the value predictions. Our computational experiments demonstrate the efficacy of CRL and LCRL across diverse instances. Our learning methods provide near-optimal solutions on small scale instances that are solved via value iteration. Furthermore, both methods outperform typical deep learning approaches such as Proximal Policy Optimization, as well as classical inventory heuristics, such as (s,S)-policy-based and Power-of-Two-based heuristics. Furthermore, LCRL achieves a 10% improvement over CRL on average, albeit with higher computational requirements. Analyses of optimal replenishment policies reveal that accounting for stochastic supply and demand influences these policies, showing the importance of our addition to the DIRP.

title: Berth and yard space allocation optimization with mobile shore power under two carbon policies
abstract: Against the backdrop of increasingly stringent global decarbonization requirements, ports, as key nodes in global trade, have attracted growing academic and industrial attention regarding both operational efficiency and carbon emissions. To improve operational efficiency and reduce carbon emissions, this study proposes a comprehensive optimization model for berth allocation, quay crane (QC) allocation, yard space allocation, and mobile shore power scheduling under two carbon policies: a carbon tax policy, which imposes a predetermined tax on carbon emissions, and a carbon trading policy, under which emission allowances can be purchased or sold relative to an allocated emission quota. The model aims to balance port operational efficiency and carbon emissions, thereby minimizing the total cost of the port. A hybrid meta-heuristic algorithm, QL-ALNS, combining Q-learning with adaptive large neighborhood search is designed to solve large-scale optimization problems. By employing Q-learning as an intelligent decision-making mechanism to adaptively select removal and repair operators, the algorithm achieves a balance between efficient exploration and exploitation of complex solution spaces. In numerical experiments, the effectiveness and efficiency of the algorithm are validated by comparing it with Gurobi and the adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model and algorithm can effectively improve port operational efficiency and reduce carbon emissions. Several managerial insights are also derived from the sensitivity analyses. For example, carbon pricing promotes emission reduction, while excessively high carbon prices or scheduling costs may increase costs without proportional environmental benefits; carbon quotas mainly affect trading costs rather than operating decisions.

title: Control irreducibility in coupled ground-aerial logistics networks: A multi-configuration simulation study
abstract: The rapid deployment of drone-based logistics introduces a critical risk: cascading failures in coupled ground-aerial networks. This study investigates whether runtime adaptive control can prevent systemic collapse when vertiports become functionally isolated due to ground traffic congestion, and where the boundary of control effectiveness lies. An integrated co-simulation framework coupling SUMO with a custom aerial logistics model is developed. Three control strategies are evaluated across 11 network configurations, complemented by a healthy baseline search and gradual stress experiments. A no-disturbance benchmark confirms operation at > 99% completion, indicating that collapse is disturbance-triggered rather than inherently infeasible. Results reveal a “Control Irreducibility” regime under strong coupling and limited capacity: none of the runtime strategies produced statistically significant improvement over baseline (paired t-test, p > .05 across all comparisons), with completion rates remaining below 4% in the stressed regime. Gradual stress experiments identify a demand-dominated transition (λ ≈ 2.0) from healthy to irreducible operation, with no intermediate controllable regime. This finding holds under alternative metrics, including effective throughput rate. Cascading collapse is consistently triggered by functional isolation, followed by overload propagation. In contrast, structural design interventions — capacity redundancy and topology-aware vertiport placement — achieve a sixfold improvement in completion rate and, when combined with adaptive control, extend network survival time by over 900 s, demonstrating design–control synergy. Validated across regular and real-world road networks, these findings establish that resilience must be embedded in network design, with runtime control serving as a complementary safety buffer.

title: The latency location-or-routing problem
abstract: This paper introduces the latency location-or-routing problem (LLoRP); a variant of the location-or-routing problem (LoRP) and an extension of the latency location-routing problem. The LLoRP consists of selecting (opening) a set of depots to serve a set of customers, which can be visited as part of routes also to be decided. The maximum number of depots to open is assumed to be exogenous. For the customers lying within a certain coverage range from an open depot, direct service is an alternative. A set of capacitated homogeneous vehicles is available to be assigned to the selected depots as needed. The goal is to minimize the sum of the waiting times of the customers for being served (latency). Several customer-centric applications of the LLoRP are discussed. Three mixed-integer-linear-programming formulations are developed and two lower bounds on the optimal latency value are devised. A tradeoff between LLoRP and LoRP is considered within a bi-objective modeling framework that is tackled using the ε − constrained method. An outcome of this analysis are compact formulations for the standard LoRP. This type of model is in itself a novelty for that problem. Finally, extensive computational results are discussed to assess the relevance of the LLoRP and the efficacy of the models and bounds proposed. The results highlight multiple distinguishing features of the LLoRP while identifying the most promising optimization models to use. They also provide strong evidence for the relevance of looking into tradeoff solutions when a cost-oriented objective becomes of interest in addition to latency.
